d7NewEntries.title: undefined() — Check if a global variable is uninitialized
d7NewEntries.principle: Use undefined() to safely check whether a global variable (prefixed with !!) has been assigned before use. Prevents BADREF errors on first access.
d7NewEntries.rule: Call undefined(!!globalVar) before accessing the variable. Returns BOOLEAN.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: lazy global initialization
if(undefined(!!ramCommonLogger)) then
  !!ramCommonLogger = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails(...) -- may throw BADREF on first call
pitfalls: undefined() only works on global variables (!! prefix), not local variables

d7NewEntries.title: !!error.text — Global error message in handle/elsehandle
d7NewEntries.principle: Inside a handle/elsehandle block, !!error.text contains the human-readable error message from the last exception.
d7NewEntries.rule: Access !!error.text only inside handle or elsehandle blocks. Contains string description of the error.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: error message capture
handle any
  !this.addErrorToList(!element.name, !attribute, 'ER13 - ' + !!error.text + !additionalMessage)
elsehandle None
  !attributeType = !currentValue.objecttype()
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !msg = !!error.text -- outside handle block returns empty or undefined
pitfalls: Only available inside handle/elsehandle blocks
PML is case-insensitive but !!Error.text and !!error.text are the same

d7NewEntries.title: MEASURE and FORMAT objects — Unit conversion and formatting
d7NewEntries.principle: MEASURE wraps a unit string and provides dbunit() for database unit conversion. FORMAT controls numeric string output including units and trailing zeros.
d7NewEntries.rule:
!measure = object MEASURE(!unitString)
!dbUnit = !measure.dbunit()
!format = object FORMAT()
!format.units = !dbUnit.string()
!format.TRAILZEROS = false
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: unit conversion with formatting
!measure = object MEASURE(!unit)
!dbUnit = !measure.dbunit()
!format = object FORMAT()
!format.units = !dbUnit.string()
!format.TRAILZEROS = false
!realValue = object REAL(!tempValue)
!result = !realValue.string(!format)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !result = !tempValue -- loses unit information
pitfalls: MEASURE requires a valid unit string
FORMAT.TRAILZEROS controls trailing zero display

d7NewEntries.title: DATETIME and DATEFORMAT objects — Timestamp generation
d7NewEntries.principle: DATETIME provides current date/time components. DATEFORMAT formats them into strings with configurable patterns.
d7NewEntries.rule:
!time = object DATETIME()
!dateFormat = object DATEFORMAT('Y_M_D')
!dateStr = !dateFormat.string(!time)
!fileName = !dateFormat.string(!time) + '_' + !time.hour().string() + ...
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: timestamp-based filename
!time = object DATETIME()
!dateFormat = object DATEFORMAT('Y_M_D')
!dateStr = !dateFormat.string(!time)
!fileName = !dateFormat.string(!time) + '_' + !time.hour().string() + !time.minute().string() + !time.second().string()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !fileName = !time.string() -- less control over format
pitfalls: DATEFORMAT pattern uses Y_M_D not YYYY-MM-DD
hour()/minute()/second() return numeric values requiring .string()

d7NewEntries.title: skip if(condition) — Conditional early loop iteration
d7NewEntries.principle: skip if(condition) skips the current iteration when the condition is true. It is a compound form of the skip statement.
d7NewEntries.rule: skip if(!condition) — equivalent to 'if (!condition) then skip endif'
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: skip pseudo attributes and unmapped columns
if(!isNameUpdate.not()) then
  skip if(!isPseudo)
endif
skip if(!isMasterUnmapped)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: if(!isPseudo) then skip endif -- more verbose than skip if(!isPseudo)
pitfalls: skip if() only works inside DO/ENDDO loops
Condition must evaluate to BOOLEAN

d7NewEntries.title: SHOW — Display a form by global reference
d7NewEntries.principle: SHOW statement displays a form identified by a global variable reference. Used to present user-facing dialogs from PML code.
d7NewEntries.rule: SHOW !!formGlobalVar — displays the form referenced by the global variable
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: show reclassification form
SHOW !!ramimportExcelReclassificationForm
!!ramimportExcelReclassificationForm.loadData(!this)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: show !localForm -- SHOW requires global variable reference
pitfalls: SHOW requires a global (!!) form reference, not a local variable
Form must be previously loaded/imported

d7NewEntries.title: displayProgress() — Show import progress bar
d7NewEntries.principle: displayProgress(current, total) displays a progress indicator in the AVEVA UI. Used for long-running import loops.
d7NewEntries.rule: Call with (current, total) parameters. PML is case-insensitive so !!displayProgress works.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!!displayProgress(1, 100)
do !i from 1 to !total
  if(!i.gt(!onePercent)) then
    !!displayProgress(!i, !total)
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_06: progress tracking in import loop
!!displayProgress(1, 100)
do !index indices !masterList
  if(!index.gt(!onePercentValue)) then
    !!displayProgress(!index, !masterList.size())
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !!displayProgress(!i) -- requires two parameters (current, total)
pitfalls: Requires two parameters: current count and total
Call sparingly to avoid UI flicker

d7NewEntries.title: Dynamic object construction via $! variable substitution
d7NewEntries.principle: The `$!varName` syntax substitutes a variable's value into command or expression text. When used as `object $!typeName()`, it dynamically creates an object of the type named by the variable's value. This is a PML1 legacy feature that coexists with PML2.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `$!typeName` only when the type name is determined at runtime. Prefer direct `object TYPE()` when the type is known at compile time.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Dynamic object creation
!type = !currentValue.objecttype()
!output = object $!type()

-- Legacy PML1 dollar substitution in command context
$!attributeName DEFAULT
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- DANGEROUS: typeName not validated
!output = object $!typeName()
pitfalls: If the variable is UNSET or BADREF, the substitution produces empty string and the construct fails silently.
The substituted value is treated as a command/expression, not a type identifier, so type safety is not enforced.

d7NewEntries.title: PML var backref query for cross-references
d7NewEntries.principle: The `var` keyword with query clauses (e.g., `backref(attname ...) of $!obj`) creates a query variable that traverses AVEVA database relationships. This is a PDMS/E3D-specific query mechanism.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always check `.set()` on var query results before accessing the variable value.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
var !queryVar queryClause of $!targetObject
if(!queryVar.set()) then
  -- process results
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Get back-references via XRPNTR attribute
var !backRefNoDetails backref(attname XRPNTR) of $!elementRefe
if(!backRefNoDetails.set()) then
  !backRefNos = !backRefNoDetails.split()
  do !backRefNo values !backRefNos
    !backRefe = !backRefNo.dbref()
    -- process back-reference
  enddo
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing .set() check
var !backRefNoDetails backref(attname XRPNTR) of $!elementRefe
!value = !backRefNoDetails -- may be BADREF
pitfalls: The `of $!targetObject` requires the target to resolve to a valid reference.
The query result may be UNSET if no back-references exist.
Split results need individual dbref() conversion.

d7NewEntries.title: AVEVA automation add-in namespace objects
d7NewEntries.principle: The `using namespace 'ModuleName'` directive allows creating objects from .NET add-in assemblies. AVEVA provides internal namespaces like RamAEUpdateElement with factory objects (CREATEELEMENT, DELETEELEMENT, UPDATEATTRIBUTE, RECLASSIFYELEMENT).
d7NewEntries.rule: Always wrap namespace object creation in handle/elsehandle blocks since .NET objects may throw exceptions.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
using namespace 'NamespaceName'
!obj = object OBJECTNAME()
handle any
  -- error handling
elsehandle none
  -- success
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
using namespace 'RamAEUpdateElement'
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elementNet.setElementTypeByName('|$!<type>|')
handle any
  !this.addErrorToList(!name, 'NAME', !!error.text)
elsehandle none
  !elementNet.addAttributeValue(|NAME|, !validName)
  !elementNet.executeSync()
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- No error handling on .NET object creation
!obj = object CREATEELEMENT()
!obj.executeSync() -- may throw
pitfalls: The namespace must be imported/available at runtime.
.NET objects may throw exceptions not caught by PML's handle any unless explicitly wrapped.
Some namespace objects require specific execution order (e.g., setElementType before execute).

d7NewEntries.title: collectAllFor with WORL scope for universal search
d7NewEntries.principle: The `!!collectAllFor(type, expression, scope)` function searches the AVEVA database for elements matching criteria. The WORL scope searches universally across all disciplines.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always check `.set()` on the result before accessing `.first()` or iterating.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Find UDA by name universally
!udaList = !!collectAllFor(|UDA|, |UPCASE(UDNAME) EQ UPCASE('MyUDA')|, WORL)
if(!udaList.set()) then
  !attributeRefe = !udaList.first()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- No set() check
!udaList = !!collectAllFor(|UDA|, |EXPRESSION|, WORL)
!target = !udaList.first() -- may fail if empty
pitfalls: WORL scope can be slow on large projects.
Expression syntax depends on AVEVA product version.
Result may be empty if no matching elements exist.

d7NewEntries.title: Pseudo attribute write access bypass in AVEVA
d7NewEntries.principle: Some AVEVA attributes (like NAME) are marked as pseudo-attributes that have special write access rules. The `isPseudo()` check allows bypassing direct attribute membership checks for these special attributes.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always combine `isPseudo()` checks with `EQNoCase('NAME')` for NAME attribute special handling.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!attribute = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName)
if(!attribute.isPseudo().not() OR !attributeName.EQNoCase('NAME')) then
  -- special handling for pseudo/NAME attributes
else
  !directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
  -- normal attribute check
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
define method .isAttributeUpdatable(!elementRefe is DBREF, !attributeName is STRING) is BOOLEAN
  !isUpdatable = false
  !attribute = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName)
  if(!attribute.isPseudo().not() OR !attributeName.EQNoCase('NAME')) then
    !isUpdatable = !this.isElementUpdatable(!elementRefe)
  else
    !directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
    !isDirectAttribute = !directAttributes.findFirst(!attributeName.upcase()).set()
    if(!isDirectAttribute) then
      !isUpdatable = !this.isElementUpdatable(!elementRefe)
    endif
  endif
  return !isUpdatable
endmethod
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing pseudo check
!directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
!isDirect = !directAttributes.findFirst(!attributeName).set()
-- NAME may pass even though not in directAttributes
pitfalls: NAME attribute is always pseudo but always updatable via element methods.
Other pseudo attributes may have different rules.
Distributed attributes bypass this check entirely.

d7NewEntries.title: SetDate of dbref — extract date from STAMP
d7NewEntries.principle: Use SetDate of dbref to extract a date value from a STAMP element.
d7NewEntries.rule: VAR !date SetDate of $!stampVar
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
!latestStamp = !stamps.first()
var !stampDate SetDate of $!latestStamp
pitfalls: STAMP must be a valid dbref; otherwise SetDate returns UNSET

d7NewEntries.title: OLD attribute qualifier for deleted element values
d7NewEntries.principle: Use OLD qualifier to retrieve the value of an attribute before an element was deleted.
d7NewEntries.rule: VAR !val OLD $!attribute of $!dbref
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
if (!action eq |DELETE|) then
  !evaluate = |var !val OLD $!expression of $!tag|
endif
$!<evaluate>
pitfalls: OLD qualifier only works for deleted elements; using it on existing elements may fail
Must use dynamic $! evaluation to pass attribute name at runtime

d7NewEntries.title: SETCOMPDATE command — set database comparison date
d7NewEntries.principle: SETCOMPDATE sets the comparison date for database queries, enabling delta detection.
d7NewEntries.rule: SETCOMPDATE FOR DB $!dbName to $!stampDate
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
var !stampDate SetDate of $!latestStamp
SETCOMPDATE FOR DB $!dbName to $!stampDate
pitfalls: Must set comparison date before collecting modified/deleted/created elements
Date must be a valid STAMP date

d7NewEntries.title: PMLTAGS object and GetListDefinition method
d7NewEntries.principle: PMLTAGS is a system object providing access to tag list definitions and database views.
d7NewEntries.rule:
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!gridDef = !!tags.GetListDefinition(!catName, !listName)
!viewName = !gridDef.DbViewName()
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!gridDef = !!tags.GetListDefinition('EQUINOR_TR3111_V7', !listName)
!sourceDbView = !gridDef.DbViewName()
pitfalls: Category name must match exactly; case-sensitive
List name must exist in the specified category

d7NewEntries.title: NetDataSource .NET object for grid data binding
d7NewEntries.principle: NetDataSource creates a .NET data source from PML arrays for binding to grid controls.
d7NewEntries.rule:
!source = object NetDataSource(name, headers, data)
!grid.BindToDataSource(!source)
d7NewEntries.syntax: NetDataSource(STRING name, ARRAY headers, ARRAY data)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
!source = object NetDataSource('$!<gridName>', !headerList, !dataList)
!dataTable.clearGrid()
!dataTable.BindToDataSource(!source)
pitfalls: headers must be ARRAY of STRING
data must be ARRAY of ARRAY (rows)
namespace must be Aveva.Core.Presentation

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL saveGridToExcel method
d7NewEntries.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL.saveGridToExcel exports the bound grid to an Excel file.
d7NewEntries.rule: !grid.saveGridToExcel(path, format, description)
d7NewEntries.syntax: saveGridToExcel(STRING path, STRING format, STRING description)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
!dataTable.saveGridToExcel('|$!publishPath$!dataFileName|', |data|, |Export delta. Author: $!<userName> Date: $!<startDateTime> Comparison Date: $!<stampDate>|)
pitfalls: Path must include file extension (.xlsx)
Format parameter determines Excel export format

d7NewEntries.title: elsehandle none — empty elsehandle as no-op
d7NewEntries.principle: elsehandle none is a valid empty handler that explicitly marks a block with no error recovery.
d7NewEntries.rule:
handle any
  -- error handling code
elsehandle none
  -- success path, no error handler needed
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
$!<evaluate>
handle any
  !rowDataList.append(!!error.text)
elsehandle none
  !rowDataList.append(!val)
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
  -- nothing
endhandle  -- missing elsehandle; implicit no-op but less explicit
pitfalls: elsehandle none is optional; omitting it is equivalent but less explicit
Do not confuse with missing elsehandle entirely in nested blocks

d7NewEntries.title: ARRAY.findFirst().set() pattern for membership testing
d7NewEntries.principle: Use findFirst() combined with .set() to test whether a value exists in an array.
d7NewEntries.rule: if (!array.findFirst(!value).set()) then ... endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_03
if (!deletedTags.findfirst(!tag).set()) then
  !action = |DELETE|
elsif (!createdTags.findfirst(!tag).set()) then
  !action = |NEW|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: if (!deletedTags.findFirst(!tag) neq UNSET) then  -- less idiomatic
pitfalls: findFirst returns UNSET if not found; .set() checks for valid result
Must use lowercase findfirst in some PML versions; check case sensitivity

d7NewEntries.title: ONERROR GOLABEL error transfer command
d7NewEntries.principle: ONERROR GOLABEL redirects macro execution to a labeled handler on error
d7NewEntries.rule: Use ONERROR GOLABEL /Label at the top of a macro to enable centralized error handling
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- ONERROR GOLABEL /Error
-- ... macro steps ...
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  -- error logging
endhandle
pitfalls: GOLABEL target must be a LABEL statement, not a label reference

d7NewEntries.title: UNCLAIM ALL PML command
d7NewEntries.principle: UNCLAIM ALL releases all claimed elements in error handlers
d7NewEntries.rule: Always call UNCLAIM ALL in error handlers to prevent element lock conflicts
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
endhandle
pitfalls: UNCLAIM ALL releases ALL claims, including those from other macros

d7NewEntries.title: unset() and badref() dbref validation
d7NewEntries.principle: Check dbref validity with unset() and badref() before accessing attributes
d7NewEntries.rule: Use (unset(:dbref) or badref(:dbref)) as guard before attribute access
d7NewEntries.syntax:
if (unset(:dbref) or badref(:dbref)) then
  -- handle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
if (unset(:TagRefToClass) or badref(:TagRefToClass)) then
  return
endif
!val = :TagRefToClass:AttributeName
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !val = :badRef:Attr -- crashes if badRef is bad
pitfalls: badref() returns true for references pointing to deleted elements
unset() returns true for null references

d7NewEntries.title: inset operator for array membership check
d7NewEntries.principle: inset checks if a value is a member of an array literal
d7NewEntries.rule: Use value inset ('A', 'B', 'C') to check membership against a list
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
if (:TagStatus inset ('ACTIVE', 'ASB', 'AFC', 'AFD')) then
  -- process
endif
pitfalls: inset is case-sensitive
array literal must use single quotes

d7NewEntries.title: ISNAMED dbref keyword
d7NewEntries.principle: ISNAMED checks if a dbref is named (has a NAME attribute)
d7NewEntries.rule: Use ISNAMED in dbref expressions to filter named elements only
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
if (ISNAMED and :TagName neq NAMN) then
  -- update
endif
pitfalls: ISNAMED cannot be used alone outside a dbref expression context

d7NewEntries.title: Attribute query with of operator
d7NewEntries.principle: The of operator queries an attribute on a dbref in expressions
d7NewEntries.rule: Use :AttributeName of :dbref to access an attribute value in expressions
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical: |:RDLSource of :ClassMappingRefToClass eq 'AKSO_Tag Properties Templates_Rev6'|
pitfalls: Attribute must exist on the dbref type
Use unset()/badref() guards before query

d7NewEntries.title: STRING.String(FORMAT) with I2 zero-padding
d7NewEntries.principle: Use STRING.String(REAL, FORMAT) to format numbers with fixed-width zero-padding
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'I2' format for 2-digit zero-padded integers
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!month = !dt.month().string('I2')
!date = !dt.date().string('I2')
!hour = !dt.hour().string('I2')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !month = !dt.month() -- no formatting, single digits
pitfalls: I2 requires the value to be a REAL or INTEGER
FORMAT is case-sensitive

d7NewEntries.title: Macro-level error handler with ONERROR + handle any
d7NewEntries.principle: Combine ONERROR GOLABEL at macro start with handle any block for centralized error recovery
d7NewEntries.rule: Place ONERROR GOLABEL /Error at top, LABEL /Error at bottom with handle any block
d7NewEntries.syntax:
ONERROR GOLABEL /Error
-- steps...
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- ONERROR GOLABEL /Error
$P --- STEP 1 ---
$P --- STEP 2 ---
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
  -- no ONERROR GOLABEL, only catches inline errors
endhandle
pitfalls: ONERROR only triggers at macro level, not within handle blocks
handle any catches all errors including those in nested calls

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL / NETDATASAVE Excel I/O workflow
d7NewEntries.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASAVE to read/write Excel files in PML macros. NETDATASAVE constructor accepts 'Grid Table' for reading or 'data' with header+data arrays for writing. NETGRIDCONTROL methods: bindToDataSource(), getrows(), gettitles(), clearGrid(), saveGridToExcel().
d7NewEntries.rule: Always import 'GridControl' with handle any before using NETGRIDCONTROL. For reading: create NETDATASAVE('Grid Table', !path), bind, call getrows()/gettitles(). For writing: create NETDATASAVE('data', !headers, !data), bind, call saveGridToExcel().
d7NewEntries.syntax:
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
!ds = object NETDATASAVE('Grid Table', !path)
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.bindToDataSource(!ds)
!rows = !grid.getrows()
!titles = !grid.gettitles()
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
!fileName = |path	o ile.xlsx|
!dataSource = object NETDATASAVE('Grid Table', !fileName)
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
!heading = !dataTable.gettitles()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Missing GridControl import will fail at runtime\n!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()  -- ERROR: GridControl not loaded
pitfalls: NETDATASAVE constructor signature differs for read vs write: 'Grid Table' (single arg) vs 'data' (3 args: header array + data array)
Always call clearGrid() before re-binding to a new data source
saveGridToExcel takes two string args: output path and data type name
Use handle any around import 'GridControl' — GridControl may not be loaded in all AVEVA sessions

d7NewEntries.title: AVEVA Elements API: CREATEELEMENT / ELEMENTTYPE workflow
d7NewEntries.principle: Use Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager namespace for dynamic element creation. CREATEELEMENT creates an element builder, ELEMENTTYPE validates element type, SetElementTypeByName sets the type, AddAttributeValue sets NAME, Execute commits. GetErrors() returns creation errors.
d7NewEntries.rule: Import |Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager| with handle any. Create element builder with object CREATEELEMENT(). Validate type with object ELEMENTTYPE(|:$!type|). If not valid, call SetElementTypeByName(). Add NAME attribute, Execute(), then GetErrors(). Always re-read dbref after creation.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
import |Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager|
handle any
endhandle
!el = object CREATEELEMENT()
!et = object ELEMENTTYPE(|:$!type|)
if (!et.valid()) then
  !el.SetElementTypeByName(|:$!type|)
endif
!el.AddAttributeValue(|NAME|, !name)
!el.Execute()
!errors = !el.GetErrors()
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
using namespace |Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager|
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()
!etype = object ELEMENTTYPE(|:$!<Type>|)
if (!etype.valid()) then
  !elementNet.SetElementTypeByName(|:$!<Type>|)
  handle any
    !msg = |Class [$!Type] is not valid|
  elsehandle none
    !elementNet.AddAttributeValue(|NAME|, !tagName)
    !elementNet.Execute()
    !errors = !elementNet.GetErrors()
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Missing namespace import causes CREATEELEMENT to be undefined\n!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()  -- ERROR without using namespace
pitfalls: ELEMENTTYPE() returns false if type is not recognized — fall back to SetElementTypeByName()
GetErrors() returns an ARRAY of error strings — iterate with do/foreach
Always re-read !tagref = !tagName.dbref() after Execute() to get a valid reference
Handle errors around Execute() — it may fail even with valid type

d7NewEntries.title: Type-gated attribute value assignment with objecttype() detection
d7NewEntries.principle: Before setting an attribute value, detect the attribute's current value type via !currentValue.objecttype(), then use the matching type conversion method: .real() for REAL, .dbref() for DBREF, .string() for STRING. Skip ARRAY types. Wrap each assignment in handle any for error recovery.
d7NewEntries.rule: Get current value: !currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attrName). Detect type: !valueType = !currentValue.objecttype(). Use if/elseif chain to match 'REAL' → .real(), 'DBREF' → .dbref(), 'STRING' → .string(). Wrap each assignment in handle any with error logging.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attrName)
!valueType = !currentValue.objecttype()
if (!valueType eq 'REAL') then
  !tagref.attribute(!attrName) = !fileValue.real()
  handle any
    !msg = |Error: $!!error.text|
  endhandle
elseif (!valueType eq 'DBREF') then
  !fileValue = |/$!fileValue|
  !tagref.attribute(!attrName) = !fileValue.dbref()
  handle any
    !msg = |Error: $!!error.text|
  endhandle
elseif (!valueType eq 'STRING') then
  !tagref.attribute(!attrName) = !fileValue.string()
  handle any
    !msg = |Error: $!!error.text|
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!valueType = !currentValue.objecttype()
if (!valueType eq 'REAL') then
  !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name()) = !fileValue.real()
  handle any
    !msg = |$!tag;$!acttype;$!attributeName1;$!fileValue;$!!error.text|
  endhandle
elseif (!valueType eq 'DBREF') then
  !fileValue = |/$!fileValue|
  !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name()) = !fileValue.dbref()
  handle any
    !msg = |$!tag;$!acttype;$!attributeName1;$!fileValue;$!!error.text|
  endhandle
elseif (!valueType eq 'STRING') then
  !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name()) = !fileValue.string()
  handle any
    !msg = |$!tag;$!acttype;$!attributeName1;$!fileValue;$!!error.text|
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Assigning without type detection can fail silently or corrupt data\n!tagref.attribute(!attrName) = !fileValue  -- No type check, may assign wrong type
pitfalls: DBREF values need |/$!fileValue| prefix before calling .dbref()
REAL conversions may fail on non-numeric strings — always wrap in handle any
ARRAY type attributes cannot be set this way — use skip or alternative approach
objecttype() returns uppercase strings: 'REAL', 'DBREF', 'STRING', 'ARRAY'

d7NewEntries.title: Dual-attribute fallback pattern for mapping table lookups
d7NewEntries.principle: When a mapping table provides two possible attribute names for a source column, attempt assignment to the primary attribute first, then fall back to the alternative attribute if the primary is invalid or the alternative name is non-empty.
d7NewEntries.rule: From mapping table, extract attributeName1 (primary) and attributeName2 (alternative). Create ATTRIBUTE objects for both. Check !attribute1.hash() gt 0 for validity. If primary fails or attributeName2 is non-empty, repeat the type-gated assignment for attribute2.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!attributeName1 = !mappingData[!mappedIdx][2]
!attributeName2 = !mappingData[!mappedIdx][3]
!attribute1 = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName1)
!attribute2 = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName2)
-- Primary assignment with error handling
if (!attribute1.hash() gt 0) then
  !currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name())
  -- type-gated assignment ...
endif
-- Fallback to alternative
if (!attributeName2.trim() neq ||) then
  if (!attribute2.hash() gt 0) then
    -- type-gated assignment ...
  endif
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!attributeName1 = !mappingData[!mappedIdx][2]
!attributeName2 = !mappingData[!mappedIdx][3]
!attribute1 = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName1)
!attribute2 = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName2)
if (!attribute1.hash() gt 0) then
  !currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name())
  -- type-gated assignment ...
endif
if (!attributeName2.trim() neq ||) then
  if (!attribute2.hash() gt 0) then
    !currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attribute2.name())
    -- type-gated assignment ...
  endif
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Skipping fallback means some columns may never get assigned\n-- when primary attribute name is invalid
pitfalls: Both attributes must be checked for hash() > 0 before assignment
Trim alternative attribute name before checking emptiness
Error messages should include both attribute names for debugging
Consider logging which attribute was successfully assigned

d7NewEntries.title: Multi-condition empty/NA/unset/zero value filtering
d7NewEntries.principle: When importing data from spreadsheets, values may appear as empty strings, 'NA', 'N/A', 'unset', or '0'. All of these should be treated as missing data and skipped. Use chained AND conditions: .empty().not() AND .lowCase() neq 'na' AND .lowCase() neq 'n/a' AND .lowCase() neq 'unset' AND value neq '0'.
d7NewEntries.rule: Check value emptiness first with !fileValue.empty().not(). Then check common placeholder strings case-insensitively with .lowCase(). Finally check numeric zero string. Only process if ALL conditions pass (value is non-empty and not a placeholder).
d7NewEntries.syntax: if (!fileValue.empty().not() and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |na| and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |n/a| and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |unset| and !fileValue neq |0|) then\n  -- process value\nendif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical: if (!fileValue.empty().not() and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |na| and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |n/a| and !fileValue.lowCase() neq |unset| and !fileValue neq |0|) then\n  !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name()) = !fileValue.real()\nendif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Only checking empty misses NA/unset values that will cause assignment errors\nif (!fileValue.empty().not()) then\n  !tagref.attribute(!attr) = !fileValue  -- May assign 'NA' string to REAL attribute
pitfalls: Use .lowCase() for case-insensitive comparison — 'NA', 'na', 'Na' are all placeholders
The .not() after .empty() is necessary — .empty() returns TRUE for empty strings
Numeric zero '0' is a valid value for some attributes but may indicate missing data in vendor imports
Consider adding 'null', 'none', '-' as additional placeholder values

d7NewEntries.title: Attribute existence validation via hash() > 0
d7NewEntries.principle: Before attempting to set an attribute value, validate that the attribute is applicable to the current element type by checking !attribute.hash() gt 0. A zero hash means the attribute is not valid for this element type.
d7NewEntries.rule: After creating ATTRIBUTE object, check !attribute.hash() gt 0. Only proceed with assignment if hash is positive. If hash is zero, log an error message indicating the attribute is not valid for this element type.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!attribute = object ATTRIBUTE(!name)
if (!attribute.hash() gt 0) then
  -- proceed with assignment
else
  !msg = |Attribute $!name is not valid for this item|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!attribute1 = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName1)
if (!attribute1.hash() gt 0) then
  !currentValue = !tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name())
  -- type-gated assignment ...
else
  !msg = |$!tag;$!attributeName1;$!fileValue;Attribute is not valid in AVEVA for this item|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Skipping hash check may cause silent failures when attribute is not valid\n!tagref.attribute(!attribute1.name()) = !fileValue  -- May fail silently if attribute not valid
pitfalls: hash() returns 0 (not an error code) when attribute is not valid
Different element types may support different sets of attributes
Always log the element tag, attribute name, and file value for debugging
This check should be done before attempting any attribute assignment

d7NewEntries.title: Special character stripping via iterative replace
d7NewEntries.principle: To clean a string of multiple special characters, split a symbol string into an array, then iterate and replace each symbol with an empty string. This is more flexible than a single replace() call when dealing with many characters.
d7NewEntries.rule: Define a symbol string containing all characters to strip. Split into array. Iterate with do/foreach. Call .replace(!symbol, '') for each. For tag names, prefix with |/$!| and call .dbref().
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!symbol = |. , - ~ * : ; _ / \ ' " & ? ! # $ % ( )|
!symbols = !symbol.split()
!symbols.append(| |)
do !symb values !symbols
  !Type = !Type.replace(!symb, '')
enddo
!tagName = |/$!<Tag>|
!tagref = !tagName.dbref()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using a single replace for each character is verbose and error-prone
!Type = !Type.replace('.', '')
!Type = !Type.replace(',', '')
!Type = !Type.replace(' ', '')  -- many more lines needed
pitfalls: Split on spaces — the symbol string should use spaces as delimiters
Remember to append a space to the symbols array (space is a common character to strip)
The backslash in the symbol string needs proper escaping in PML
This pattern is useful for tag names and element type names

d7NewEntries.title: Element creation via Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager
d7NewEntries.principle: Use CREATEELEMENT and ELEMENTTYPE objects to create elements with typed attributes in AVEVA Engineering.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create ELEMENTTYPE with class name, validate name() is not UNKNOWN, then call SetElementTypeByName, AddAttributeValue, Execute, and GetErrors.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!et = object ELEMENTTYPE('|:$<ClassName>|')
if (!et.name() neq |UNKNOWN|) then
  !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|:$<ClassName>|')
  !elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !tagName)
  !elem.Execute()
  !errors = !elem.GetErrors()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!et = object ELEMENTTYPE('|:$!<Type>|')
if (!et.name() neq |UNKNOWN|) then
  !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|:$!<Type>|')
  !elem.AddAttributeValue(|NAME|, !tag)
  !elem.Execute()
  !errors = !elem.GetErrors()
  DO !error values !errors
    !err = |$!tag;NA;NA;$!error|
    !issueData.append(!err.split(|;|))
  ENDDO
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Creating element without type validation
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elem.SetElementTypeByName('|:$!<Type>|')  -- crashes if type is unknown
!elem.Execute()
pitfalls: Always check ELEMENTTYPE.name() neq UNKNOWN before calling SetElementTypeByName
GetErrors() returns an ARRAY of error strings — iterate to log them
CREATEELEMENT is in Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager namespace, not a builtin
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA Engineering PML Customization — Database Interfaces

d7NewEntries.title: Display progress with !!displayProgress
d7NewEntries.principle: Use !!displayProgress(current, total) in loops to show progress in AVEVA UI.
d7NewEntries.rule: Call !!displayProgress(!current, !total) inside DO loops to update the user-facing progress indicator.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
DO !row values !data
  !rowIdx = !data.findFirst(!row)
  !!displayProgress(!rowIdx, !data.size())
ENDDO
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- No progress shown in long loops
DO !row values !data
  -- no progress update
ENDDO
pitfalls: !!displayProgress is a global helper function, not a method of a specific object
First argument should be current iteration count, second should be total

d7NewEntries.title: STRING to DBREF conversion via .dbref() method
d7NewEntries.principle: Convert a STRING variable to a DBREF using the .dbref() method for database element references.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !tagName.dbref() where !tagName is a STRING in the format /$<element_path> to obtain a DBREF.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!tag = |/$!<Tag>|
!tagRef = !tag.dbref()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using dbref command instead of method
DBREF !tagRef /path/to/element  -- PML1 style, not PML2 method
pitfalls: The string must be in valid element path format (e.g., /$<Type>/<Name>)
The referenced element must exist or be creatable in the current session scope
DBREF conversion does not validate element existence — handle errors after use
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA Engineering PML Customization — PML Expressions

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASOURCE for Excel import/export
d7NewEntries.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASOURCE objects to read/write Excel files in PML macros.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create NETGRIDCONTROL, bind to NETDATASOURCE with file path, call getrows()/gettitles(), iterate data, write results back via clearGrid + BindToDataSource + saveGridToExcel.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !fileName)
!grid.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !grid.getrows()
!heading = !grid.gettitles()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing import for GridControl
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()  -- fails without import 'GridControl'
pitfalls: Must import 'GridControl' with handle any/endhandle
NETDATASOURCE constructor signature: NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', fileName) for read, NETDATASOURCE('data', headers, data) for write
saveGridToExcel requires the data argument to match the NETDATASOURCE name

d7NewEntries.title: Type-gated attribute value assignment
d7NewEntries.principle: Before assigning an attribute value, check the attribute type (objecttype) and use the appropriate conversion method (real(), string(), dbref()).
d7NewEntries.rule: Obtain attribute value via !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()), check objecttype(), then assign using the matching conversion method within a handle any block.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!currentValue = !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name())
!valType = !currentValue.objecttype()
if (!valType eq 'REAL') then
  !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal.real()
endif
if (!valType eq 'STRING') then
  !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal.string()
endif
if (!valType eq 'DBREF') then
  !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = (!fileVal).dbref()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!currentValue = !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name())
!valType = !currentValue.objecttype()
if (!valType eq 'REAL') then
  !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal.real()
  handle any
    !err = |$!tag;$!col;$!fileVal;$!!error.text|
    !issueData.append(!err.split(|;|))
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Assigning without type check
!tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal  -- may fail if types mismatch
pitfalls: Always check objecttype() before assigning — different types need different conversion methods
Wrap each type-gated assignment in handle any to catch conversion failures
ARRAY type attributes should be skipped (not assigned via simple assignment)
DBREF values need / prefix prepended before .dbref() conversion

d7NewEntries.title: Special character stripping from type names
d7NewEntries.principle: Strip invalid characters from element type names using iterative replace() over a character list.
d7NewEntries.rule: Define a symbol string containing all invalid characters, split into an array, iterate with DO/ENDDO, calling replace() on each symbol.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!sym = |. , - ~ * : ; _ / \ ' " & ? ! # $ % ( )|
!symList = !sym.split()
!symList.append(| |)
!symList.append('|')
DO !symb values !symList
  !typeRaw = !typeRaw.replace(!symb, '')
ENDDO
!typeRaw = !typeRaw.trim()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Single replace call misses other characters
!type = !type.replace(|. , - ~|, '')  -- only removes first occurrence of the whole substring
pitfalls: Must iterate over individual characters, not replace the whole string at once
Trim() after stripping to remove leading/trailing whitespace
The en-dash (‐) character is Unicode and must be copied exactly from source
Pipe character (|) must be appended separately as it may not appear in the split

d7NewEntries.title: SAVEWORK and UNCLAIM ALL macro cleanup commands
d7NewEntries.principle: End Excel-driven element modification macros with SAVEWORK to commit changes and UNCLAIM ALL to release database claims.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place SAVEWORK followed by UNCLAIM ALL at the end of macros that modify elements to ensure all changes are committed and no database locks remain.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!reportGrid.saveGridToExcel(!feedbackFile, |data|)

SAVEWORK
UNCLAIM ALL
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing SAVEWORK
!reportGrid.saveGridToExcel(!feedbackFile, |data|)
-- macro ends without SAVEWORK — changes may not persist
pitfalls: SAVEWORK must follow the last element-modifying operation
UNCLAIM ALL releases all claimed elements — do not use if you need to keep claims
Both should be at the very end of the macro

d7NewEntries.title: Attribute hash validation before assignment
d7NewEntries.principle: Use attribute.hash() to verify that an attribute name is valid for the target element before attempting to set its value.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create ATTRIBUTE object, check hash() > 0, then proceed with value assignment. Log errors for invalid attributes.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!attr = object ATTRIBUTE(|$!col|)
if (!attr.hash() gt 0) then
  !tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal
else
  !err = |Attribute [$!col] is not valid in AVEVA|
  !issueData.append(!err.split(|;|))
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_newtag_import.pmlmac
!attr = object ATTRIBUTE(|$!col|)
if (!attr.hash() gt 0) then
  -- proceed with assignment
else
  !err = |$!tag;$!col;$!fileVal;Attribute [$!col] is not valid in AVEVA|
  !issueData.append(!err.split(|;|))
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- No hash check before assignment
!attr = object ATTRIBUTE(|$!col|)
!tagRef.attribute(!attr.name()) = !fileVal  -- may silently fail
pitfalls: hash() returns 0 for non-existent attributes — always check before assignment
System attributes (prefixed with :) and UDAs both return valid hashes
Empty attribute names return hash 0
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA Engineering PML Customization — Attribute Class

d7NewEntries.title: PMLTAGS object and exportasxls method
d7NewEntries.principle: The PMLTAGS object provides methods to query and export engineering tag data to spreadsheet formats.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create a PMLTAGS instance with `object PMLTAGS()`, then call `.exportasxls(!groupName, !listName, !filePath)` to export matching tags.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Export tags from a named list
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |my-list|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
    !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
    var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
    !!tags.exportasxls(!gName, '$!<gridRef.LSTNAM>', '$!outPath')
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't reuse PMLTAGS across different export contexts without clearing
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!!tags.exportasxls(...)
!!tags.exportasxls(...) -- stale state may cause wrong export
pitfalls: PMLTAGS is specific to AVEVA Engineering; it may not be available in PDMS-only environments.
The exportasxls method requires valid group and list names; passing empty strings causes runtime errors.

d7NewEntries.title: inset operator for list membership in PML1 queries
d7NewEntries.principle: The `inset` operator tests whether a value is a member of a list of values in PML1 query expressions.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `value inset (list1, list2, ...)` in PML1 query expressions to test membership. Combine with `NOT` to exclude values.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Exclude tags with VOID or Future status
!tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED'
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use inset with PML2 method chaining
!status.inset(...) -- incorrect, use infix form
pitfalls: inset is a PML1 infix operator; it works inside query expression strings but not in PML2 object method chains.
Values inside inset must be pipe-delimited strings.

d7NewEntries.title: LSTDEF and LSTGRP objects for list management
d7NewEntries.principle: LSTDEF (List Definition) and LSTGRP (List Group) are AVEVA Engineering objects used to manage named lists for tag data grouping.
d7NewEntries.rule: Query LSTDEF to find a list by name. Access LSTGRP via `LSTGRP of` to get the group. Use CATNAM to get the group name. Set lstflt to clear filters.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |listName|)
!gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
!gridRef.lstflt = !realUnset
var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Find and clear a list
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |IM-tag-dataset|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
    !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
    !gridRef.lstflt = ARRAY()
    var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: -- Don't assume grid.size() == 1; always check before accessing first()
pitfalls: LSTDEF/LSTGRP are Engineering-specific; not available in PDMS.
lstflt is a reference attribute; setting it to an empty ARRAY clears the filter.

d7NewEntries.title: DATETIME object with .string() format codes
d7NewEntries.principle: The OBJECT DATETIME() construct returns a datetime object with methods for year, month, date, hour, minute, second. Each can be formatted via .string(formatCode).
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `.string('I2')` for zero-padded 2-digit integers, `.string('I4')` for 4-digit years. Format codes follow PDMS/E3D FORMAT conventions.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Build a timestamped filename
!dt = OBJECT DATETIME()
!ts = !dt.year().string() & '-' & !dt.month().string('I2') & '-' & !dt.date().string('I2')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use .string() without format code for zero-padding
!month = !dt.month().string() -- may produce single-digit '3' instead of '03'
pitfalls: Format codes like 'I2' are PDMS/E3D FORMAT codes; their exact behavior may vary by product version.
.year() returns a REAL; .string() on a bare REAL may not zero-pad.

d7NewEntries.title: matchwild function in PML1 query expressions
d7NewEntries.principle: The `matchwild` function in PML1 query expressions performs wildcard pattern matching on attribute values or names.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `matchwild(attribute, |pattern|)` inside PML1 query expression strings. Supports `*` (any chars) and `?` (single char).
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Find tags matching a pattern
!tagFilter = 'ISNAMED and matchwild(name, |*GB.*|)'
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use matchwild as a STRING method in query strings
matchwild(!name, |*|) -- incorrect, use PML1 infix form
pitfalls: matchwild in query strings is PML1-style; the STRING.MatchWild() method is PML2-style. They are not interchangeable in query expression strings.
Variable interpolation in matchwild patterns requires `$!var` syntax inside pipe strings.

d7NewEntries.title: undefined() function for global variable existence check
d7NewEntries.principle: Use undefined() to check if a global variable has been assigned before accessing it.
d7NewEntries.rule: undefined(!!globalVar) returns TRUE if the global is unassigned, FALSE if assigned.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_addErrorToList
if(undefined(!!ramCommonLogger)) then
  !!ramCommonLogger = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Accessing unassigned global without check
!!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails(...) -- may crash if not initialized
pitfalls: Only works with global variables (!!), not local variables (!)

d7NewEntries.title: STRING.unset() method for existence check
d7NewEntries.principle: Use unset() on STRING or ARRAY to check if the variable has been assigned a value.
d7NewEntries.rule: unset() returns TRUE if the variable is unassigned/undefined, FALSE if it holds a value.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!str.unset() -- TRUE if !str is not set
!arr.unset() -- TRUE if !arr is not set
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_loadReportDetails
if(!viewDetails.set() AND !viewDetails.size().eq(7)) then
  -- process details
else
  !this.clearData()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Checking set() vs unset() confusion
if(!str.unset()) then -- wrong: checks if unset, but code expects set
  ...
pitfalls: set() and unset() are inverses: !x.set() is equivalent to !x.unset().not()

d7NewEntries.title: OBJECT.objecttype() method for runtime type identification
d7NewEntries.principle: Use objecttype() on any PML2 object to get its type name as a STRING at runtime.
d7NewEntries.rule: objecttype() returns a STRING containing the object type identifier.
d7NewEntries.syntax: !this.objecttype() -- returns the type name of the current object
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_addErrorToList
!!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails(!this.objecttype(), !errorList)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Hardcoding type names instead of using objecttype()
!!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails('JACEISDELIVERYMANAGER', !errorList)
pitfalls: Returns the declared type name, not the variable name

d7NewEntries.title: BLOCK evaluate with !evalIndex special variable
d7NewEntries.principle: When evaluating a BLOCK on an ARRAY, !evalIndex is a special variable available inside the block that holds the current index.
d7NewEntries.rule: !columns.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!columns[!evalIndex].string()|)) iterates over !columns, with !evalIndex set to each index.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_columnCollection
!columnRefNos = !columns.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!columns[!evalIndex].string()|))
-- CB obj_09_loadReport
!headings = !headings.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!headings[!evalIndex][1]|))
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using a regular loop instead of evaluate
DO !i FROM 1 TO !columns.Size()
  !result.Append(!columns[!i].string())
ENDDO
pitfalls: !evalIndex is only available inside the BLOCK expression, not outside
BLOCK evaluates each element; the result is an ARRAY of the evaluated values

d7NewEntries.title: PROJECT CODE system variable with !!evar()
d7NewEntries.principle: PROJECT CODE is a PML1 system query variable that returns the current PDMS project code. Use !!evar() to evaluate it in PML2 context.
d7NewEntries.rule: !!evar(|PDMSUSER|) returns the PDMS user data path. !!evar(!varName + |DFLTS|) returns the project defaults path.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_readConfiguration
!!filePath = !!evar(|PDMSUSER|) + |\EISConfiguration.xlsx|
if(!file.exists().not()) then
  var !projectCode PROJECT CODE
  !filePath = !!evar(!projectCode + |DFLTS|) + |\EISConfiguration.xlsx|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using hardcoded paths instead of system variables
!filePath = 'C:\\project\\defaults\\config.xlsx'
pitfalls: PROJECT CODE requires being in a PDMS session context
DFLTS path depends on PDMS installation configuration

d7NewEntries.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
d7NewEntries.principle: Reload a previously-defined PML object before creating instances to ensure the latest code is loaded.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `PML RELOAD OBJECT <name>` before `!var = object <name>()` when the object may have been updated since the session started.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.alarmsDataUpdate()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.alarmsDataUpdate()
pitfalls: RELOAD only works for objects previously defined in the current session (via .pmlobj file loaded earlier).
RELOAD does not work for system objects.
If the object has been modified externally, RELOAD is necessary to pick up changes without restarting AVEVA.

d7NewEntries.title: PML macro file header comment patterns
d7NewEntries.principle: Macros use comment headers to record source path and metadata. PML1 uses `--$m` with path; PML2 recommends `$*` comments.
d7NewEntries.rule: Prefer `$*` for inline-safe comments. Use `--$m "path"` in legacy macros for path tracking.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
$* Factory benchmark generated from semantic source summary only for mac_01
$* Source path: docs/codebase/macros/alarm_refresh.pmlmac

PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: --$m "C:\Users\ADZV\OneDrive - Ramboll\AVEVA_SERVER\Addons\PMLLIB\RAM\Engineering\jackdow\run-macro\alarm_refresh.pmlmac"
pitfalls: `--$m` is a PML1 legacy pattern; `$*` is preferred in new code.
Path comments in `--$m` format may contain OneDrive/cloud-sync paths that break in production environments.
Do not copy absolute OneDrive paths into shared benchmarks.

d7NewEntries.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
d7NewEntries.principle: PML RELOAD OBJECT reloads an object definition from disk; use before constructing instances to ensure fresh definitions.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use `PML RELOAD OBJECT <objectName>` before `!var = object <objectName>()` when the object definition may have changed.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_02
define object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
  member .name is STRING
endobject

PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.defineAreasForCables()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.defineAreasForCables()  -- stale definition may be used
pitfalls: PML RELOAD OBJECT only reloads from disk; if the object was defined inline in the same macro, it has no file to reload from.
Reloading a user-defined type does not automatically update existing instances of that type.

d7NewEntries.title: Macro file header comment conventions
d7NewEntries.principle: Use `$*` comment lines for macro headers; they are safe inline and after commands. Legacy `--$m` header with quoted path is PML1 style.
d7NewEntries.rule: Replace `--$m "path/to/file.pmlmac"` with `$*` comment lines describing the macro purpose.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
$* cable-area-update.pmlmac
$* Reloads TAGMANAGEMENTTMP and invokes defineAreasForCables().
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.defineAreasForCables()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
--$m "C:\path\to\cable-area-update.pmlmac"
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.defineAreasForCables()
pitfalls: `--$m` with a path is a PML1 legacy convention; `$*` is the canonical PML2 comment style.
The `--$m` comment may contain a file path that is stale or environment-specific.

d7NewEntries.title: Custom methods on user-defined object types
d7NewEntries.principle: User-defined objects (e.g., TAGMANAGEMENTTMP) may have project-specific methods not covered by system KB. Method signatures must be verified from source.
d7NewEntries.rule: When calling methods on user-defined objects, ensure the method exists in the object definition. Document custom methods in KB.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.defineAreasForCables()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.nonExistentMethod()  -- method not defined on type
pitfalls: User-defined object methods are not discoverable through system KB; they must be verified against the `.pmlobj` source.
Method names on user-defined types are case-insensitive in PML but should follow project conventions.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: Methods on User-Defined Object Types KB

d7NewEntries.title: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP Object
d7NewEntries.principle: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP is a custom/external object used for tag management operations including alarm updates and class name updates.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always PML RELOAD OBJECT before creating instances of TAGMANAGEMENTTMP to ensure latest method definitions are loaded.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.GetMappingData()
!tagMgmt.ClassNameUpdate(boolean)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.GetMappingData()
!tagMgmt.ClassNameUpdate(true)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()  -- missing RELOAD OBJECT first
!tagMgmt.ClassNameUpdate(true)
pitfalls: Skipping PML RELOAD OBJECT may cause stale method definitions.
ClassNameUpdate expects a boolean argument; omitting it causes runtime error.

d7NewEntries.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT Directive
d7NewEntries.principle: PML RELOAD OBJECT reloads a PML object definition from its source, ensuring the latest version is available for instantiation.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT before creating instances of custom or addon objects that may have been updated.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical: PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
pitfalls: RELOAD OBJECT only affects objects loaded via PML; objects defined in .pmlobj files may need different reload mechanisms.
Repeated reloads without cleanup may cause memory leaks for some object types.

d7NewEntries.title: namn — PDMS object name pseudo-attribute
d7NewEntries.principle: The 'namn' pseudo-attribute returns the PDMS name of an object. It is accessed as 'namn of $!ref' or via substitute expression '$!ref.namn'.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'var !name namn of $!ref' or '$!ref.namn' in pipe strings. Alias for 'name' in some PDMS versions.
pitfalls: 'namn' is a PDMS-specific spelling; E3D may use 'name' instead. Use '$!ref.namn' for maximum compatibility.

d7NewEntries.title: dtxr — PDMS description-text pseudo-attribute
d7NewEntries.principle: The 'dtxr' pseudo-attribute returns the description text of a PDMS object. Used as a fallback when 'desc' is unavailable.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'var !desc dtxr of $!ref' to retrieve the description text. Typically used as a fallback after 'desc of $!ref' fails.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB EBA_full_tag_export.pmlmac
var !desc desc of $!item
handle any
    var !desc dtxr of $!item
endhandle
pitfalls: 'dtxr' may be empty if no description is set. Always check UNSET before using.

d7NewEntries.title: GridControl .NET add-in for Excel export
d7NewEntries.principle: The GridControl add-in provides NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASOURCE objects for building tabular data and exporting to Excel.
d7NewEntries.rule: Import GridControl, use 'handle any' for the import, create NETDATASOURCE with header/data arrays, bind to NETGRIDCONTROL, then call saveGridToExcel().
d7NewEntries.syntax:
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
!source = object NETDATASOURCE('data', !headers, !data)
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.BindToDataSource(!source)
!grid.saveGridToExcel(!path)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB EBA_full_tag_export.pmlmac
using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.clearGrid()
!source = object NETDATASOURCE('data', !headerList, !dataList)
!dataTable.BindToDataSource(!source)
!dataTable.saveGridToExcel(|$!<publishPath>$!<dataFileName>|)
pitfalls: NETDATASOURCE 'data' mode requires header array as second argument.
saveGridToExcel accepts a full file path including extension.
Namespace may be 'Aveva.Core.Presentation' or 'Aveva.Pdms.Presentation' depending on E3D version.

d7NewEntries.title: collect all with multiple PDMS class names and filters
d7NewEntries.principle: The 'collect all' query can target multiple PDMS class names in one expression, optionally with a filter clause.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'var !items collect all (CLASS1 CLASS2 CLASS3) with (FILTER)' to collect objects across multiple types in a single query.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB EBA_full_tag_export.pmlmac
var !items collect all (EQUI SUBE STRUC FRMW SBFR PIPE HVAC CWAY SUPPO BRAN MEM) with (ISNAMED)
pitfalls: ISNAMED filter excludes unnamed objects.
Large class sets can be slow; consider restricting scope with site/zone filters.

d7NewEntries.title: FINISH directive — macro termination
d7NewEntries.principle: The FINISH directive explicitly terminates a PML macro execution and returns control to the calling context.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place FINISH at the end of a macro to signal clean completion. Equivalent to implicit end-of-file termination but makes intent explicit.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB EBA_full_tag_export.pmlmac
!dataTable.saveGridToExcel(|$!<publishPath>$!<dataFileName>|)

FINISH
pitfalls: FINISH in a macro is optional — the macro ends at EOF. Use it to clarify intent.

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASOURCE for Excel/CSV data import
d7NewEntries.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE to import spreadsheet data into PML macros. GridControl add-in must be imported before use.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always import 'GridControl' with error handling before creating NETGRIDCONTROL instances.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Import Excel data into PML
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !filePath)
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
!heading = !dataTable.gettitles()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()  -- GridControl not imported
pitfalls: GridControl add-in must be installed and accessible in the AVEVA environment
NETDATASource constructor varies by add-in version
Aveva.Core.Presentation namespace required for NETGRIDCONTROL

d7NewEntries.title: CREATEELEMENT and ELEMENTTYPE for programmatic element creation
d7NewEntries.principle: Use CREATEELEMENT to create new PDMS/E3D elements programmatically. Set the element type via ELEMENTTYPE or SetElementTypeByName before adding attributes and executing.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always validate ELEMENTTYPE before calling SetElementTypeByName. Check GetErrors() after Execute().
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!etype = object ELEMENTTYPE('|<typeName>|')
if (!etype.valid()) then
  !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|<typeName>|')
  !elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !name)
  !elem.Execute()
  !errors = !elem.GetErrors()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()
!etype = object ELEMENTTYPE('|$!<class>|)
if (!etype.valid()) then
  !elementNet.SetElementTypeByName('|$!<class>|)
  !elementNet.AddAttributeValue(|NAME|, !tagName)
  !elementNet.Execute()
  !errors = !elementNet.GetErrors()
  do !error values !errors
    !msg = |$!tag;$!error|
  enddo
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !name)
!elem.Execute()  -- No element type set
pitfalls: ELEMENTTYPE must match a valid AVEVA class name
SetElementTypeByName by string name is more forgiving than ELEMENTTYPE constructor
GetErrors() returns an array that must be iterated

d7NewEntries.title: Chained STRING methods: replace().trim(), findfirst(), lowcase()
d7NewEntries.principle: STRING objects support method chaining in PML2. Common patterns include replace().trim() for data cleaning and findfirst() for array searching.
d7NewEntries.rule: Chain .replace().trim() for cleaning input strings. Use .findfirst() to search ARRAY of strings.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!tag = !row[!nameId].replace(|-|, |-|).trim()
!class = !row[!classId].replace(|-|, |-|).trim()
!nameId = !heading.findfirst(|NAME|)
if (!class.lowcase() neq |unset|) then
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !tag = trim(!row[!nameId])  -- trim is method, not function
pitfalls: findfirst returns an index value, not a boolean — use .set() to test validity
replace takes two pipe-delimited strings: search pattern and replacement
lowcase() returns a copy, does not modify in place

d7NewEntries.title: Nested handle blocks and scoping in PML
d7NewEntries.principle: PML handle blocks can be nested. Inner handle blocks take precedence for errors within their scope. elsehandle must match its corresponding handle.
d7NewEntries.rule: Each handle must have a matching endhandle. Nested handles should be clearly indented. elsehandle none catches no errors (acts as pass-through).
d7NewEntries.syntax:
handle any
  -- operations that may fail
  handle any
    -- inner operations
  endhandle
elsehandle none
  -- inner failure recovery
endhandle
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
handle any
  !elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
  if (!etype.valid()) then
    !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|TYPE|')
  else
    !msg = |Error: invalid type|
  endif
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
  !elem = object CREATEELEMENT()  -- missing endhandle
elsehandle any  -- orphaned elsehandle
pitfalls: elsehandle none catches zero errors — it is not the same as elsehandle any
Nested handle scoping can be confusing — prefer flattening when possible
Using namespace inside handle block may not persist after handle ends

d7NewEntries.title: FINISH directive to terminate macro execution
d7NewEntries.principle: FINISH is a macro directive that immediately terminates execution of the current macro. It is the equivalent of exit in a form context.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use FINISH at the end of macros that have completed their work or encountered a fatal error.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!IssueFile.Close()
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !IssueFile.Close()  -- macro continues executing after this
pitfalls: FINISH terminates the entire macro, not just the current block
Do not use FINISH in form methods — use RETURN or exit instead
FINISH is macro-specific, not available in all PML contexts

d7NewEntries.title: Паттерн: обработка ошибок при экспорте в Excel через exportasxls
d7NewEntries.principle: Экспортные макросы должны оборачивать вызовы exportasxls в handle any/endhandle и логировать ошибки вместо молчаливого игнорирования.
d7NewEntries.rule: Обернуть каждый вызов !!tags.exportasxls в handle any/endhandle; в catch-блоке записать ошибку в логгер; продолжать обработку следующих элементов.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical: -- NOT FOUND IN SOURCES — pattern missing from current codebase
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- CB EBE_full_tag_export.pmlmac:
-- !!tags.exportasxls('100 ADMIN','$!gridName','$!path')
-- $* БЕЗ handle: ошибка экспорта прервёт весь макрос
pitfalls: exportasxls может частично записать файл при ошибке — проверить .exists() после экспорта
Путь с пробелами требует экранирования в $!<...>

d7NewEntries.title: Проверка существования директории перед экспортом
d7NewEntries.principle: Перед записью файла в каталог необходимо проверить его существование и создать при необходимости.
d7NewEntries.rule: Использовать FILE.exists() или SYSCOM для проверки/создания директории перед экспортом.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!dirObj = object FILE('$!exportFolder')
if !dirObj.exists().not() then
  SYSCOM |mkdir "$!exportFolder"|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical: -- NOT FOUND IN SOURCES — pattern missing from current codebase
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- CB EBE_full_tag_export.pmlmac:
-- !publishPath = 'C:\Users\...\_AUEDB_export\'
-- $* БЕЗ проверки: если папка удалена, экспорт упадёт
pitfalls: Путь с пробелами требует двойных кавычек в SYSCOM
mkdir не создаёт вложенные папки — нужен recursive mkdir

d7NewEntries.title: Dollar-m ($m) metadata comment in PML macros
d7NewEntries.principle: Macros often include a --$m or $* $m comment line with the original file path for traceability. This is a convention, not a PML command execution.
d7NewEntries.rule: When embedding $m in a macro header, use $* $m "path" format in benchmarks. The original may use --$m "path" as a full-line comment.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
--$m "C:\path\to\original\macro.pmlmac"
PML RELOAD OBJECT MYOBJECT
!obj = object MYOBJECT()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Do not execute $m as a command when it is intended as metadata.
pitfalls: $m is both a command (run macro) and a metadata marker in comments. Context determines intent.
In benchmarks, convert --$m to $* $m for inline-safe comment format.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide — Dollar Special Symbols

d7NewEntries.title: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP.EquipmentNameUpdate(boolean) method
d7NewEntries.principle: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP is a user-defined object type with multiple update methods (alarmsDataUpdate, ClassNameUpdate, EquipmentNameUpdate). Each takes a boolean parameter.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create TAGMANAGEMENTTMP instance via 'object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()' and call update methods with boolean arguments.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.EquipmentNameUpdate(false)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Do not assume TAGMANAGEMENTTMP has no-argument constructor — always use 'object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()'.
pitfalls: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP methods like EquipmentNameUpdate, ClassNameUpdate, alarmsDataUpdate all take boolean parameters.
The boolean parameter typically controls force/overwrite behavior.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide — Object Methods

d7NewEntries.title: $m metadata comment convention in PML macro headers
d7NewEntries.principle: Macros may include a --$m or $* $m comment line with the original file path for traceability. This is a human convention, not a PML command execution. The $m in this context is distinct from the PML $M command (which loads and runs a macro file).
d7NewEntries.rule: When embedding $m in a macro header, use -- $m "path" format in original macros. In benchmarks, convert to $* $m "path" for inline-safe comment format.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- $m "C:\path\to\original\macro.pmlmac"
!data = object array()
var !sites collect all SITE
do !siteName values !sites
  !siteRef = !siteName.dbref()
enddo
pitfalls: $m (lowercase) in comments is a metadata marker convention; $M (uppercase) is a PML command that loads and runs a macro file.
Do not execute $m as a command when it is intended as metadata in a comment line.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide — Dollar Special Symbols

d7NewEntries.title: ONERROR / GOLABEL / LABEL error trap in PML macros
d7NewEntries.principle: PML1 macros use ONERROR to redirect control to a named LABEL; the LABEL is paired with a handle block for cleanup.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place ONERROR GOLABEL /LabelName at the top of the macro. Define LABEL /LabelName near FINISH. Inside the label, use handle any to capture the error context and perform cleanup (SAVEWORK, UNCLAIM ALL, logging).
d7NewEntries.syntax:
ONERROR GOLABEL /LabelName
...
LABEL /LabelName
handle any
  -- cleanup
endhandle
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
ONERROR GOLABEL /Error
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
...
do !item values !list
  -- work
enddo
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!logger.writeError(...)
endhandle
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Missing ONERROR — errors crash the macro
import 'GridControl'
do !item values !list
  -- no error handling
enddo
FINISH
pitfalls: ONERROR must be placed before any import or using statements.
LABEL name must match exactly (case-insensitive but spelling must match).
FINISH must come after the error handler label block.

d7NewEntries.title: SAVEWORK and UNCLAIM ALL PDMS commands in PML macros
d7NewEntries.principle: SAVEWORK saves current database state; UNCLAIM ALL releases all element claims. Used in error recovery to prevent database lock.
d7NewEntries.rule: Call SAVEWORK before UNCLAIM ALL in error handlers. UNCLAIM ALL should be called to release any element claims that may have been acquired during processing.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(...)
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ UNCLAIM ALL without SAVEWORK — data loss risk
LABEL /Error
handle any
  UNCLAIM ALL
  -- SAVEWORK missing: unsaved changes lost
endhandle
pitfalls: SAVEWORK is slow on large databases — consider conditional save.
UNCLAIM ALL releases ALL claims; use UNCLAIM !ref for selective release.

d7NewEntries.title: PML1 inset and matchwild operators in query expressions
d7NewEntries.principle: PML1 provides set-membership (inset) and wildcard matching (matchwild) operators for query expressions in COLLECT ALL and other query commands.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use inset for membership testing: VALUE inset (|A|, |B|). Use matchwild for wildcard string matching: matchwild(string, pattern).
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
!tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED'
!tagFilter = !tagFilter & 'matchwild(namn of :TagRefToMCPackage, |*$!<commPckg.namn>*|)'
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Using 'in' instead of 'inset'
!result = !value in (|A|, |B|)  -- not valid PML
pitfalls: inset expects a parenthesised list of values, not an array.
matchwild pattern uses * for any characters and ? for single character.
matchwild is a function call, not an operator — use matchwild(string, pattern).

d7NewEntries.title: 2D array initialization in PML
d7NewEntries.principle: PML arrays can be indexed with multiple subscripts: array[i][j] for 2D data. Initialize by assigning individual cells.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create the array with ARRAY(), then assign cells using !arr[i][j] = value. There is no native 2D array literal — each cell must be assigned individually.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
!commonAttributes = object ARRAY()
!commonAttributes[1][1] = ':RAMTagOwner'
!commonAttributes[1][2] = 'Tag Owner'
!commonAttributes[2][1] = ':TagStatus'
!commonAttributes[2][2] = 'Tag Status'
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ JavaScript-style 2D literal (not valid PML)
!arr = [['a','b'], ['c','d']]
pitfalls: PML ARRAY does not support multi-dimensional literals — each cell must be assigned.
Subscript indices start at 1, not 0.
Appending to a 2D array requires careful management of the outer array size.

d7NewEntries.title: COLLECT ALL with $! variable substitution in filter expressions
d7NewEntries.principle: PML allows $! variable substitution inside COLLECT ALL filter strings, enabling dynamic queries inside loops.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use $!varName inside the COLLECT ALL with () expression to substitute the current loop variable's value into the filter string.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
do !item values !list
  !filter = 'attribute eq |$!<item.attr>*|'
  var !results collect all (TYPE) with ($!filter)
  -- process results
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
do !commPckgName values !commPckgList
  !commPckg = !commPckgName.dbref()
  !tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED and matchwild(namn of :TagRefToMCPackage, |*$!<commPckg.namn>*|)'
  var !tagList collect all (ENGITE) with ($!tagFilter)
enddo
pitfalls: $! substitution only works inside pipe-delimited strings within COLLECT ALL expressions.
Variable must be a simple reference — method chains like $!<item.method()> are not supported.
Ensure the loop variable is resolved before the COLLECT ALL executes.

d7NewEntries.title: FINISH keyword in PML macros
d7NewEntries.principle: FINISH terminates macro execution cleanly. It should be placed at the end of the macro, after any error handler LABEL.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place FINISH as the last statement in the macro, after the error handler LABEL block. FINISH ensures clean exit and resource release.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
LABEL /Error
handle any
  -- error cleanup
endhandle
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(...)
endhandle
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Code after FINISH (never executes)
FINISH
-- This line is unreachable
pitfalls: FINISH after LABEL means the label block is only reachable via ONERROR GOLABEL, not via normal flow.
If FINISH is placed before the error handler, the error handler is dead code.

d7NewEntries.title: STRING .after() method for substring extraction
d7NewEntries.principle: STRING objects provide .after() method to extract substring after a delimiter
d7NewEntries.rule: !result = !str.after(|delimiter|) returns the portion of string after the first occurrence of delimiter
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
!name = |/RAM/MyView|
!afterSlash = !name.after(|/|)
$P Result: $!afterSlash
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !afterSlash = !name.substring(|/|)  -- not valid PML
pitfalls: Returns empty string if delimiter not found
Case-sensitive delimiter matching

d7NewEntries.title: DELETE member MEM command with dollar substitution
d7NewEntries.principle: DELETE $!<member>.type MEM removes all members of a specified type
d7NewEntries.rule: DELETE $!<obj>.type MEM deletes all elements/members of the type specified by the dollar-substituted member
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
!dbViewGroup = /RAM_IM_DBViewGroup
DELETE $!<dbViewGroup.type> MEM
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: DELETE !dbViewGroup.type MEM  -- missing $ prefix for substitution
pitfalls: $! required for variable substitution in command context
MEM keyword required

d7NewEntries.title: Handle specific numeric error code tuples
d7NewEntries.principle: PML allows handling specific error code tuples (major, minor) with handle (major,minor)
d7NewEntries.rule: handle (major,minor) catches only that specific error combination; multiple elsehandle tuples can be chained
d7NewEntries.syntax:
handle (majorCode,minorCode)
  -- error handler
elsehandle (majorCode2,minorCode2)
  -- alternative handler
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
handle (68,5)
  $P ERROR: element exists in list
elsehandle (99,532)
  $P ERROR: element does not exist
elsehandle (99,534)
  $P ERROR: long name
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: handle 68  -- incomplete error code, may not match
pitfalls: Error codes are (major, minor) tuple, not single number
Order matters: first matching handler wins

d7NewEntries.title: elsehandle none for no-error branch
d7NewEntries.principle: elsehandle none explicitly handles the 'no error' path within a handle block
d7NewEntries.rule: elsehandle none executes when no error occurred; useful for conditional logic after error-prone operations
d7NewEntries.syntax:
handle any
  -- error recovery
elsehandle none
  -- no error occurred, original state preserved
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
handle any
  DELETE ATTCOLUMN
  NEW EXPCOLUMN
  -- fallback creation
elsehandle none
  -- no error, keep original ATTCOLUMN
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: elsehandle  -- missing 'none', may cause syntax error
pitfalls: elsehandle none is different from omitting elsehandle
Semantically means 'no error branch' not 'catch all'

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL from Aveva.Core.Presentation
d7NewEntries.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL is a .NET add-in object for displaying tabular data in PML
d7NewEntries.rule: Import GridControl, use namespace Aveva.Core.Presentation, create object NETGRIDCONTROL(), use clearGrid(), bindToDataSource(), getrows()
d7NewEntries.syntax:
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.clearGrid()
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.clearGrid()
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !fileName)
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: NETGRIDCONTROL  -- missing 'object' keyword and namespace
pitfalls: Requires 'import GridControl' before use
Requires 'using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|'
NETDATASOURCE is a separate object

d7NewEntries.title: NETDATASOURCE for Excel/data binding
d7NewEntries.principle: NETDATASOURCE provides data source for NETGRIDCONTROL, can read from Excel files
d7NewEntries.rule: object NETDATASOURCE('DataSourceName', filePath) binds external data to grid control
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
!fileName = |C:\data\source.xlsx|
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !fileName)
