!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: NETDATASOURCE('name')  -- missing file path argument
pitfalls: Requires GridControl add-in loaded
File path must be valid and accessible

d7NewEntries.title: DbView (DBVW) creation and configuration commands
d7NewEntries.principle: DbView objects are created with NEW DBVW, configured with DESC/UDNA/AUTCRE/ALWDEL/ELEL commands
d7NewEntries.rule: NEW DBVW → DESC → UDNA → AUTCRE → ALWDEL → ELEL REM ALL → configure sub-objects (EXPFIL/EXPCOL/ATTCOL)
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!dbView = !name.dbref()
NEW DBVW $!name
DESC |description|
UDNA |udname|
AUTCRE TRUE
ALWDEL TRUE
ELEL REM ALL
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
!dbView = !dbViewName.dbref()
handle any
  NEW DBVW $!dbViewName
  !dbViewUdname = !dbViewDesc.replace(|-|, | |)
  DESC |$!dbViewUdname|
  UDNA |$!dbViewUdname|
  AUTCRE TRUE
  ALWDEL TRUE
  ELEL REM ALL
  !dbView = !!ce
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: NEW DBVW !name  -- missing $ prefix for variable
pitfalls: Must use $! for variable substitution in command context
AUTCRE/ALWDEL require TRUE/FALSE values
ELEL REM ALL clears existing element list

d7NewEntries.title: DbView sub-objects: EXPFILTER, EXPCOLUMN, ATTCOLUMN
d7NewEntries.principle: DbViews contain sub-objects for expressions, columns, and filters created with NEW commands
d7NewEntries.rule: NEW EXPFILTER → EXPRESSION → EXPTYPE; NEW EXPCOLUMN → DESC → UDNA → EXPRESSION → EXPTYPE → UTYP; NEW ATTCOLUMN → DESC → UDNA → DBATTRIBUTE
d7NewEntries.syntax:
NEW EXPFILTER
EXPRESSION |expr|
EXPTYPE 'PML'

NEW EXPCOLUMN
DESC |name|
UDNA |udname|
EXPRESSION |expr|
EXPTYPE 'PML'
UTYP $!<dataType>

NEW ATTCOLUMN
DESC |name|
UDNA |udname|
DBATTRIBUTE $!<attr>
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
NEW EXPCOLUMN
DESC |$!<name>|
UDNA |$!<name>|
if (!value.matchwild(|*!*|)) then
  !value = $!<value>
endif
EXPRESSION |$!<value>|
EXPTYPE 'PML'
UTYP $!<dataType>
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: EXPRESSION !value  -- missing $ prefix and | delimiters
pitfalls: EXPTYPE requires quoted string 'PML'
UTYP requires $! substitution for data type variable
DESC and UDNA require | pipe delimiters for strings

d7NewEntries.title: ELEL ADD and ELEL REM commands for DbView element lists
d7NewEntries.principle: ELEL commands manipulate element lists within DbView objects
d7NewEntries.rule: $!<viewName> ELEL ADD $!<element> adds an element; ELEL REM ALL removes all elements
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
$!<dbViewName> ELEL ADD $!<value>
handle (68,5)
  $P ERROR ELE $!<value> IS EXIST IN ELELIST
elsehandle (99,532)
  $P ERROR ELE $!<value> IS NOT EXIST
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: ELEL ADD !value  -- missing $ prefix and view context
pitfalls: Requires $!<viewName> prefix for context
Error codes (68,5), (99,532), (99,534) are specific to ELEL operations

d7NewEntries.title: STRING .replace() method for text substitution
d7NewEntries.principle: STRING objects provide .replace(old, new) method for text substitution
d7NewEntries.rule: !result = !str.replace(|oldText|, |newText|) returns string with all occurrences of oldText replaced by newText
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
!dbViewUdname = !dbViewDesc.replace(|-|, | |)
$P Converted: $!dbViewUdname
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !result = !str.replace('-',' ')  -- single quotes not valid PML pipe strings
pitfalls: Use | pipe delimiters for string arguments
Replaces all occurrences, not just first

d7NewEntries.title: UTYP command for setting data type in DbView columns
d7NewEntries.principle: UTYP command sets the data type for expression and attribute columns in DbView
d7NewEntries.rule: UTYP $!<dataType> assigns the data type variable to the current column context
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
NEW EXPCOLUMN
DESC |$!<name>|
UDNA |$!<name>|
EXPRESSION |$!<value>|
EXPTYPE 'PML'
UTYP $!<dataType>
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: UTYP !dataType  -- missing $ prefix for substitution
pitfalls: Requires $! variable substitution
Must be used within EXPCOLUMN or ATTCOLUMN context

d7NewEntries.title: Data-driven macro template pattern with multi-type dispatch
d7NewEntries.principle: Macros can drive behavior from Excel data by reading rows and dispatching on parameter type codes
d7NewEntries.rule: Read Excel via NETGRIDCONTROL/NETDATASOURCE → iterate rows → check parameterType field → execute corresponding command block
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
do !row values !data
  !param = !row[2]
  if (!param eq |TYPE1|) then
    -- type 1 processing
  elseif (!param eq |TYPE2|) then
    -- type 2 processing
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_20
do !row values !data
  !parameterType = !row[2]
  if (!parameterType eq |1_ELEL| and !dbView.set()) then
    $!<dbViewName> ELEL ADD $!<value>
  endif
  if (!parameterType eq |2_EXPFIL| and !dbView.set()) then
    NEW EXPFILTER
    EXPRESSION |$!<value>|
    EXPTYPE 'PML'
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: for !row in !data  -- not valid PML, use DO/ENDDO
pitfalls: Each conditional uses !dbView.set() to ensure context is set
Parameter type codes are strings requiring | delimiters
Multiple independent if blocks (not elseif) allow multiple actions per row

d7NewEntries.title: DbView sub-object types: ELEL, EXPFIL, ATTFIL, EXPCOL, ATTCOL
d7NewEntries.principle: DbView objects expose sub-objects (elements, expression filters, attribute filters, expression columns, attribute columns) that can be queried via !!CollectAllFor with type filter and $!dbView scope.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL'|'ATTFIL'|'EXPCOL'|'ATTCOL', ||, $!dbView) to collect DbView sub-objects scoped to a specific DbView instance.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Collect all EXPFIL under a DbView
!expList = !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL', ||, $!dbView)
do !exp values !expList
  !expr = !exp.Expression
  !type = !exp.ExpType
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- WRONG: Collecting EXPFIL without DbView scope
!badList = !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL', ||, world) -- returns ALL EXPFIL in world, not scoped
pitfalls: Scope must use $!dbView reference, not just the DbView name
Each sub-object type has different attributes — check type-specific properties

d7NewEntries.title: DbView .elel property for element iteration
d7NewEntries.principle: DbView objects expose a .elel property that returns the list of elements included in the view.
d7NewEntries.rule: Access !dbView.elel to iterate through elements of a DbView. Each element is a DBREF.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
do !ele values !dbView.elel
  !string = !dbViewName & |;1_ELEL;;| & !ele & |;;|
  !data.append(!string.split(|;|))
enddo
pitfalls: !ele is a DBREF, not a string — concatenate with string for CSV output

d7NewEntries.title: Handle NONE for var command recovery
d7NewEntries.principle: When a PML var command (like ATTDEF query) may fail due to missing or invalid references, wrap in handle none to provide a fallback value instead of aborting the macro.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use handle none (without error codes) when the var command is optional and a fallback value is acceptable. The handler assigns a default value to the variable.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
if (!condition) then
  var !result OBJECT $!<reference> ATTR1 ATTR2
  handle none
    !result = !defaultValue
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
if (!udName.unset() or !udName.empty()) then
  var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME TYPE RPTX SIZE DEFI DTYP UNIT VISI QSET QTXT ITYP DESTEX
  handle none
    !udName = !attData[3]
  endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- WRONG: handle any on optional var command
var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME
handle any
  !udName = !attData[3]
endhandle -- handle any catches ALL errors including programming mistakes
pitfalls: handle none catches ALL errors including typos — use only when fallback is intentional
var result array indexing (!attData[3]) depends on attribute order

d7NewEntries.title: NETDATASOURCE + NETGRIDCONTROL Excel export pattern
d7NewEntries.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE to create tabular data views and export to Excel. NETDATASOURCE takes a name, header array, and data array.
d7NewEntries.rule: 1) Create NETGRIDCONTROL object. 2) Create NETDATASOURCE with header list and data array. 3) Bind data source to grid. 4) Call saveGridToExcel with file path.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.clearGrid()
!source = object NETDATASOURCE('data', !headerList, !data)
!dataTable.BindToDataSource(!source)
!dataTable.saveGridToExcel(|$!dataFile|)
pitfalls: NETDATASOURCE constructor signature: (name, headers, data) — headers must be an ARRAY, data must be an ARRAY of arrays or strings
saveGridToExcel accepts file path as pipe-delimited string with $! variable substitution
import 'GridControl' with handle ANY tolerance is recommended — NETGRIDCONTROL may not be available in all environments

d7NewEntries.title: String .unset() and .empty() methods
d7NewEntries.principle: PML string objects provide .unset() and .empty() methods for validation. .unset() checks if the variable is unset/BADREF. .empty() checks if the string is empty or whitespace.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !str.unset() to check BADREF/unset state. Use !str.empty() to check for empty/whitespace content. Combine with .or() for guard conditions.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
if (!str.unset() or !str.empty()) then
  -- handle missing or empty value
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
if (!udName.unset() or !udName.empty()) then
  var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME TYPE RPTX SIZE DEFI DTYP UNIT VISI QSET QTXT ITYP DESTEX
  handle none
    !udName = !attData[3]
  endhandle
endif
pitfalls: .unset() returns TRUE if the variable is BADREF or never assigned
.empty() returns TRUE for empty strings and whitespace-only strings

d7NewEntries.title: PMLTAGS object and GetListDefinition
d7NewEntries.principle: PMLTAGS is the entry point for AVEVA Engineering Tags API. GetListDefinition retrieves a list definition by name and grid reference.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !!tags = object PMLTAGS() then !!tags.GetListDefinition(listName, gridName) to access list metadata.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!gridDef = !!tags.GetListDefinition('15.2 Leirvik Data Export', !listName)
!sourceDbView = !gridDef.DbViewName()
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !!tags.GetListDefinition without creating object first
pitfalls: GetListDefinition requires valid list name and grid reference
DbViewName() returns the DbView reference, not a string

d7NewEntries.title: DbView sub-object types: ATTCOL and EXPCOL
d7NewEntries.principle: ATTCOL (attribute column) and EXPCOL (expression column) are sub-objects within a DbView. Access via .dbref() to get .udname or .DbAttribute.
d7NewEntries.rule: var !fields collect all (ATTCOL EXPCOL) for $!dbView, then iterate with do !field values !fields.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
var !fields collect all (ATTCOL EXPCOL) for $!sourceDbView
do !field values !fields
  !udname = !field.dbref().udname
  !expression = !field.dbref().DbAttribute
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
!fields = collect all (ATTCOL EXPCOL) for $!sourceDbView
do !field values !fields
  !udname = !field.dbref().udname
  !expression = !field.dbref().DbAttribute
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Collecting ATTCOL without DbView scope
pitfalls: .DbAttribute may throw (2,201) if attribute is not directly accessible — fall back to .expression
.udname is always available on ATTCOL/EXPCOL

d7NewEntries.title: OLD prefix for delta queries on ENGITEM
d7NewEntries.principle: The OLD keyword before 'collect all' queries the delta (deleted/modified) state of ENGITEM objects. Combined with MODIFIED(), DELETED(), CREATED() predicates.
d7NewEntries.rule: var !deletedTags OLD collect all (ENGITEM) with ( DELETED() ) to get deleted tags.
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Using OLD without predicate — returns all items, not just delta
pitfalls: MODIFIED() and DELETED() require OLD prefix; CREATED() does not
OLD queries the comparison state set by SETCOMPDATE

d7NewEntries.title: SETCOMPDATE STAMP for tag comparison context
d7NewEntries.principle: SETCOMPDATE STAMP sets the comparison date context so that OLD collect queries return delta data relative to a specific stamp.
d7NewEntries.rule: SETCOMPDATE STAMP $!latestStamp where !latestStamp is a STAMP object reference.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
var !stamps collect all STAMP
!latestStamp = !stamps[2]
SETCOMPDATE STAMP $!latestStamp
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
var !stamps collect all STAMP
!latestStamp = !stamps[2]
SETCOMPDATE STAMP $!latestStamp
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Using SETCOMPDATE without prior STAMP collection
pitfalls: Index 2 skips the most recent stamp (index 1)
SETCOMPDATE affects all subsequent OLD collect queries

d7NewEntries.title: NetDataSource 3-argument constructor with headers and data
d7NewEntries.principle: NetDataSource accepts (name, headers, data) where headers is an array of column names and data is a 2D array of rows.
d7NewEntries.rule: !source = object NetDataSource('$!<gridName>', !headerList, !dataList) where !dataList is ARRAY of ARRAY.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
!source = object NetDataSource('$!<gridName>', !headerList, !dataList)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Passing flat array as data — causes column misalignment
pitfalls: Data must be ARRAY of ARRAY (each row is an ARRAY)
Header count must match column count in each row

d7NewEntries.title: findfirst().set() pattern for array membership testing
d7NewEntries.principle: Array.findfirst(item) returns the first matching element; .set() checks if a value was assigned, confirming membership.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use (!deletedTags.findfirst(!tag).set()) to test if a tag exists in the deleted array.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
if (!deletedTags.findfirst(!tag).set()) then
  !action = |DELETE|
elseif (!createdTags.findfirst(!tag).set()) then
  !action = |NEW|
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Using findfirst() without .set() — always truthy even if no match
pitfalls: findfirst returns the matched element or UNSET; .set() distinguishes these

d7NewEntries.title: Syscom MKDIR for directory creation
d7NewEntries.principle: Syscom executes system commands. MKDIR creates directories. Use with variable substitution for dynamic paths.
d7NewEntries.rule: Syscom |MKDIR "$!publishPath"| to create a directory from a PML variable path.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_22
!publishPath = '$!<folder>$!year-$!month\'
Syscom |MKDIR "$!publishPath"|
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: Using MKDIR without quotes around variable path
pitfalls: Syscom MKDIR may fail silently if directory already exists
Use !!mkdir() function as alternative in PML2

d7NewEntries.title: DATETIME system object — year(), month(), date(), hour(), minute() methods
d7NewEntries.principle: The DATETIME object provides date/time component extraction via method calls on an OBJECT DATETIME() instance.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always create via OBJECT DATETIME(), then chain component methods. Use .string('I2') for zero-padded 2-digit formatting.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_fullDataProperties-export.pmlmac
!dt = OBJECT DATETIME()
!year = !dt.year()
!month = !dt.month().string('I2')
!date = !dt.date().string('I2')
!hour = !dt.hour().string('I2')
!minute = !dt.minute().string('I2')
pitfalls: DATETIME object not documented in official KB. Methods must be confirmed against AVEVA docs or real source.
.string('I2') format specifier not in official syntax reference but confirmed in codebase.

d7NewEntries.title: $!<var> variable interpolation in pipe-delimited strings
d7NewEntries.principle: PML supports $!<variable> syntax for interpolating local/global variable values into pipe-delimited strings at macro execution time.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use $!<varname> inside |...| strings to embed variable values. For attribute references use $!/attribute.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_fullDataProperties-export.pmlmac
!publishPath = |C:\...\TagPropertyValue_full_extract_$!<year>-$!<month>-$!<date>-$!<hour>.xlsx|
-- CB LoopData.pmlobj
!logFile = |$!<this.pathName>\$!logName|
pitfalls: $!<var> vs $!var: angle brackets are used for local variables in some contexts; $!name per syntax reference is for command substitution.
Mixing $!<var> and $!name in the same string is valid but may cause confusion.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Syntax — Dollar special symbols

d7NewEntries.title: --$m macro metadata comment — source path tracking
d7NewEntries.principle: The --$m comment on line 1 of a macro file records the full source path of the macro, typically for development tracking and debugging.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place --$m with the full quoted path as the first line of any macro file. This is a comment, not an executable directive.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_fullDataProperties-export.pmlmac
--$m "C:\Users\ADZV\OneDrive - Ramboll\AVEVA_SERVER\Addons\PMLLIB\RAM\Engineering\jackdow\_publish\macro\JDE_fullDataProperties-export.pmlmac"
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: $M "C:\path\to\macro.pmlmac"
pitfalls: Do not confuse --$m (comment) with $M (macro execution command).
The $M command executes a macro file; --$m is purely a metadata comment.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Syntax — Dollar special symbols

d7NewEntries.title: Extracting tag/element properties via !!ce dot notation
d7NewEntries.principle: Macros that need tag metadata should use !!ce as the current-element reference and access attributes via dot notation (.name, .desc, .acttype).
d7NewEntries.rule: Always assign !!ce to a local !var first to avoid repeated pseudo-variable lookups. Use !local naming for all extracted properties.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!tag = !!ce
!tagName = !tag.name
!tagDescription = !tag.desc
!tagActtype = !tag.acttype
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !!ce.name -- accessing !!ce directly multiple times without caching
pitfalls: If the current element is not a tag type, .desc or .acttype may return empty or error.
Consider adding BADREF checks if the macro may run on non-tag elements.

d7NewEntries.title: COLL ALL PML1 declarative collection query
d7NewEntries.principle: COLL ALL is the PML1 declarative syntax for querying all elements of a given type from the database, with optional WITH clause for filtering.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use COLL ALL (TYPE) WITH (conditions) to build a collection variable. Compound conditions use eq, neq, inset, NOT, EMPTY, ISNAMED, etc.
d7NewEntries.syntax: var !varName COLL ALL (ElementType) WITH (:Attr1 eq |value1| and :Attr2 neq |value2|)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
var !tags COLL ALL (ENGITEM) WITH (:TagStatus eq |ACTIVE| and ISNAMED and NOT(EMPTY(:RAMTAGOWNER)) and :RAMTAGOWNER eq |LEIR|)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: var !tags = !!collectallfor('engitem', '|ACTIVE|', !!ce)  -- PML2 procedural form, different semantics
pitfalls: COLL ALL returns STRING array of element references, not DBREF objects
Each element in the result is a STRING that must be converted via .dbref()
The WITH clause uses PML1 attribute syntax (:AttrName)

d7NewEntries.title: do ... values loop for array iteration
d7NewEntries.principle: The 'do ... values' construct iterates over each element value in an array, assigning the value to the loop variable.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'do !var values !array' to iterate over array values. This is the idiomatic PML loop for iterating array elements by value (not index).
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
do !tagString values !tags
    !tagRef = !tagString.dbref()
    -- process !tagRef
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
do !i from 1 to !tags.size()
    !tagString = !tags[!i]  -- index-based, less idiomatic
enddo
pitfalls: Loop variable is a STRING copy, not a reference
Cannot modify the original array from within the loop
Nested with do ... from ... to requires careful index management

d7NewEntries.title: inset() string containment function
d7NewEntries.principle: inset() checks whether a string value is contained in a list of string values.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use inset(string, |val1|, |val2|, ...) to test if the string matches any of the listed values. Returns TRUE or FALSE.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
LOWCASE(:TagClassName) inset(|gas detector|, |heat detector|, |junction box|)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: :TagClassName eq |gas detector| or :TagClassName eq |heat detector|  -- verbose equivalent
pitfalls: inset() is case-sensitive; use LOWCASE() or UPCASE() for case-insensitive matching
Only available in PML1 WITH clause expressions

d7NewEntries.title: IFT() conditional function
d7NewEntries.principle: IFT() is a PML inline conditional function: IFT(condition, trueValue, falseValue).
d7NewEntries.rule: Use IFT(test, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse) for inline conditional logic in expressions.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
!expression = IFT(!mappingRowRef.:RDLDabaconExpression.unset() or !mappingRowRef.:RDLDabaconExpression.empty(), !attributeEntry.:RDLDabaconExpression, !mappingRowRef.:RDLDabaconExpression)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
if (!condition) then
    !result = |true_val|
else
    !result = |false_val|
endif  -- longer form
pitfalls: All three arguments are evaluated before the function call — no short-circuit evaluation
Return type is ANY; may need explicit type handling

d7NewEntries.title: BLOCK object with evaluate() for dynamic PML expressions
d7NewEntries.principle: The BLOCK object wraps a PML expression string and can be evaluated against a DBREF to produce a runtime value.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'object BLOCK(expressionString)' to create a block, then 'dbref.evaluate(block)' to compute the result.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
!block = object BLOCK(!expression)
!value = !tagRef.evaluate(!block)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !value = !tagRef.:AttributeName  -- static attribute access only
pitfalls: Expression string must be valid PML syntax
Handle exceptions with handle ANY around evaluate() call
Returns ANY type; may be STRING, REAL, or ERROR

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL object methods: clearGrid, BindToDataSource, saveGridToExcel
d7NewEntries.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL is a .NET add-in object for displaying tabular data in PML. Key methods include clearGrid(), BindToDataSource(), and saveGridToExcel().
d7NewEntries.rule: Create NETGRIDCONTROL, clearGrid(), bind NETDATASOURCE, then optionally saveGridToExcel() for export.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.clearGrid()
!source = object NETDATASOURCE(label, headers, data)
!grid.BindToDataSource(!source)
!grid.saveGridToExcel(path)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.clearGrid()
!source = object NETDATASOURCE('data', !headerList, !dataList)
!dataTable.BindToDataSource(!source)
!dataTable.saveGridToExcel(|$!publishPath|)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !grid = object array()  -- ARRAY is not NETGRIDCONTROL
pitfalls: Requires 'import GridControl' and 'using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|'
NETDATASOURCE label parameter is a string identifier
saveGridToExcel() path must be a valid file path string

d7NewEntries.title: OBJECT DATETIME() constructor and accessor methods
d7NewEntries.principle: OBJECT DATETIME() creates a datetime object. Access year, month, date, hour, minute via accessor methods.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !dt = OBJECT DATETIME() then !dt.year(), !dt.month(), etc. Convert to formatted string with .string('format').
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
!dt = OBJECT DATETIME()
!year = !dt.year()
!month = !dt.month().string('I2')
!date = !dt.date().string('I2')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !year = !!datetime.year()  -- incorrect global reference
pitfalls: .string('I2') pads with leading zero for single-digit months/days/hours
Available as PML2 object; verify PML1 equivalent if needed

d7NewEntries.title: Nested handle ANY inside do loops for per-iteration error recovery
d7NewEntries.principle: A handle ANY block can be nested inside a do loop to catch and recover from errors per-iteration without aborting the entire loop.
d7NewEntries.rule: Wrap per-iteration risky operations in handle ANY. Set fallback values in the handler. Use endhandle to close the block.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
do !i values !array
    handle any
        !result = |fallback value|
    endhandle
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
if (!expression.unset().not() or !expression.empty().not()) then
    !block = object BLOCK(!expression)
    !value = !tagRef.evaluate(!block)
    handle any
        !value = 'Error when calculating value as per expression [$!attributeEntry.:RDLDabaconExpression] for element [$!tagRef.name]. Error: $!!error.text'
    endhandle
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
    do !i values !array
        -- entire loop in one handler
    enddo
endhandle  -- catches too broadly
pitfalls: Nested handle ANY inside outer handle ANY requires careful scoping
!!error.text is available only within the handler block
Always set a fallback value in the handler to avoid UNSET propagation

d7NewEntries.title: NETDATASOURCE + NETGRIDCONTROL data-binding workflow
d7NewEntries.principle: Use NETDATASOURCE to bind an external data file to a NETGRIDCONTROL, then retrieve rows via getrows() for iteration.
d7NewEntries.rule: import |GridControl| with handle/elsehandle; create NETDATASOURCE with grid table name and file path; create NETGRIDCONTROL; call bindToDataSource then getrows; iterate with DO...VALUES.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !fileName)
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
do !row values !data
  ... ENDDO
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_tagProperties_upload.pmlmac
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !fileName)
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
do !row values !data
  !Tag = !row[1]
  !EngCon = !row[2]
  !InsCon = !row[3]
enddo
pitfalls: NETDATASOURCE constructor first arg is the table/grid name, not the file path.
getrows() may return UNSET if the file is empty or unreadable — always check .Unset().
GridControl must be imported before use.

d7NewEntries.title: dbref tag reference with attribute read/write via .:AttributeName
d7NewEntries.principle: Use |$!<var>| to build a tag reference string, resolve with .dbref(), then read/write attributes via .:AttributeName notation.
d7NewEntries.rule: !tagName = |$!<Tag>|; !tagref = !tagName.dbref(); !tagref.:RAMTAGOWNER = !value
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_tagProperties_upload.pmlmac
!tagName = |$!<Tag>|
!tagref = !tagName.dbref()
!tagref.:RAMTAGOWNER = !EngCon
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !tagref = !Tag.dbref()  -- Tag must be a string reference, not a raw value
pitfalls: dbref() requires a properly formatted tag reference string (e.g., |$!<Tag>|).
Attribute name after .: must be a valid system or UDA attribute.
Reading a non-existent attribute may raise an exception — wrap in handle/elsehandle.

d7NewEntries.title: Dollar-string interpolation $! and $< for tag references
d7NewEntries.principle: Use $! for variable substitution and $< for tag/element reference construction within pipe-delimited strings.
d7NewEntries.rule: |$!<variable>| expands variable value into a tag reference; $!!error.text accesses error object text.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_tagProperties_upload.pmlmac
!tagName = |$!<Tag>|
!tagref = !tagName.dbref()
!issueMsg = |$!<Tag>;$!!error.text|
pitfalls: $! and $< only work inside pipe-delimited strings.
$!!error.text must be accessed within a handle/elsehandle block.

d7NewEntries.title: FINISH statement placement in error handlers
d7NewEntries.principle: FINISH should be placed inside the error handler block to stop macro execution after error logging.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place FINISH inside handle/.../endhandle to halt on error. Do not rely on commented-out FINISH or place it after endhandle as dead code.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  -- error recovery actions
  FINISH
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Correct: FINISH inside error handler
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  !!logger.writeError('macro failed')
  FINISH
endhandle

-- Anti-pattern: FINISH as comment
--FINISH

-- Anti-pattern: FINISH after endhandle (unreachable)
endhandle
FINISH
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  --FINISH
endhandle
FINISH
pitfalls: FINISH inside handle block stops macro; FINISH after endhandle is unreachable if the handle block completes normally.
Commented-out FINISH (--FINISH) is silently ignored and does not stop macro on error.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide - Macro Error Handling

d7NewEntries.title: String delimiters required in error handler function calls
d7NewEntries.principle: All string arguments to PML functions must use pipe delimiters (|text|) even inside error handlers.
d7NewEntries.rule: Always wrap string literals in pipe delimiters in function call arguments, including in error handler blocks.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Correct: pipe-delimited string argument
!!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(|/project/output/log.xlsx|, false)

-- Anti-pattern: bare path without delimiters
!!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(/project/output/log.xlsx, false)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(/project/output/log.xlsx, false)
pitfalls: Paths without string delimiters may parse as variable substitutions or cause syntax errors.
Error handlers are often written hastily and may omit delimiters that are present in main code.

d7NewEntries.title: Custom LOOPDATA object usage pattern
d7NewEntries.principle: Custom user-defined objects (e.g. LOOPDATA) are reloaded via PML RELOAD OBJECT, instantiated with object(), and used via method chaining. Path assignment and SaveLog are typical property/method patterns.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT <Name> before instantiating a custom object. Wrap method calls in handle/any blocks for error resilience.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
handle any
  PML RELOAD OBJECT <ObjectName>
endhandle
!obj = object <ObjectName>()
handle any
  !obj.Method()
endhandle
!obj.property = |value|
handle any
  !obj.SaveLog(|filename.xlsx|, false)
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
$* loop-create.pmlmac
handle any
  PML RELOAD OBJECT LOOPDATA
endhandle
!loop = object LOOPDATA()
handle any
  !loop.GetData()
endhandle
handle any
  !loop.LoopCreate()
endhandle
!loop.pathName = |C:\Temp\loop-create-log|
handle any
  !loop.SaveLog(|loop-create-log.xlsx|, false)
endhandle
exit
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!loop = object LOOPDATA()
!loop.GetData()
!loop.LoopCreate()
!loop.pathName = |C:\Temp\test|
!loop.SaveLog(|test.xlsx|, false)
pitfalls: LOOPDATA is a RAM-specific custom object; not a built-in PML type
PML RELOAD OBJECT is required before object() instantiation for custom types
SaveLog second argument (false) controls overwrite behavior — must match caller intent

d7NewEntries.title: LOOPDATA Object — Data Export and Logging
d7NewEntries.principle: LOOPDATA is an AVEVA system object for exporting loop data and instrument field information to external files.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT LOOPDATA before instantiation. Create with object LOOPDATA(), then call GetData(), InstrumentFieldDataTransfer(), set pathName, and call SaveLog() to export.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB loop-data-update.pmlmac
PML RELOAD OBJECT LOOPDATA
!loop = object LOOPDATA()
!loop.GetData()
!loop.InstrumentFieldDataTransfer(FALSE)
!loop.pathName = |C:\path\to\log|
!loop.SaveLog(|loop-data-update-log.xlsx|, FALSE)
pitfalls: LOOPDATA must be reloaded before use in a new PML session.
pathName must point to a writable directory.
SaveLog second argument controls overwrite behavior; FALSE means do not overwrite.

d7NewEntries.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
d7NewEntries.principle: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT to reload a PML object definition from the library before creating instances, ensuring the latest version is loaded.
d7NewEntries.rule: Place PML RELOAD OBJECT <ObjectName> before object <ObjectName>() in macros that depend on custom object definitions. This is necessary when the object may have been updated in the library without a server restart.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB manual-valve-description.pmlmac
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern: !tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()  -- may use stale object definition
pitfalls: PML RELOAD OBJECT is a command, not a PML statement — it does not use = assignment.
The object must exist in the PMLLIB library path; otherwise the reload silently succeeds but object() may fail.
In production macros, wrap object() and method calls in HANDLE/ENDHANDLE for safety.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA E3D PML Customization Guide — Macro Programming

d7NewEntries.title: Macro error handling pattern — HANDLE/ENDHANDLE around object operations
d7NewEntries.principle: Wrap object instantiation and method calls in HANDLE/ENDHANDLE blocks to prevent silent failures.
d7NewEntries.rule: After object() construction and before calling methods on custom objects, use: handle any ... endhandle to catch and report errors.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
handle any
  -- error recovery or logging
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
handle any
  !tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
  handle any
    !tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')
  endhandle
endhandle
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')  -- no error handling
pitfalls: Nested HANDLE/ENDHANDLE blocks can mask errors from inner blocks if the outer handler catches 'any'.
Using HANDLE ANY on object() may hide library-load issues; consider checking the result before method calls.
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA E3D PML Customization Guide — Error Handling

d7NewEntries.title: Минимальный макрос: reload + instantiate + call без boilerplate
d7NewEntries.principle: Не все макросы требуют import/handle/переменных; минимальный паттерн — комментарий-путь → PML RELOAD OBJECT → object NAME() → метод — валиден и встречается в production.
d7NewEntries.rule: Минимальный макрос: (опц.) --$m комментарий → PML RELOAD OBJECT <имя> → !var = object <имя>() → !var.метод() ; error-handling и import-guard отсутствуют намеренно.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
--$m "path/to/macro.pmlmac"
PML RELOAD OBJECT OBJECTNAME
!obj = object OBJECTNAME()
!obj.someMethod()
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
--$m "C:\Users\ADZV\OneDrive - Ramboll\AVEVA_SERVER\Addons\PMLLIB\RAM\Engineering\jackdow\run-macro\pipeSupport-refresh.pmlmac"
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.pipeSupportDataUpdate()
pitfalls: Отсутствие error handling означает, что ошибки propagate вверх по стеку вызовов
TAGMANAGEMENTTMP должен быть загружен (pml rehash + pml reload) до вызова
Минимальный макрос не защищает от отсутствующих зависимостей

d7NewEntries.title: PMLTAGS Object for Engineering Tag Export
d7NewEntries.principle: PMLTAGS is a system object providing methods to export engineering tag data to XLSX format via GridControl integration.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create via object PMLTAGS(), then call exportasxls(groupName, listName, filePath) to export a list definition's data.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB RAMBiReportExport.pmlmac
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!!tags.exportasxls(!gridGroupName, '$!<gridRef.LSTNAM>', '$!filepath')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!tags = PMLTAGS()  -- missing OBJECT keyword
!!tags.exportxls(...)  -- wrong method name
pitfalls: Must use OBJECT keyword before PMLTAGS()
exportasxls requires valid LSTDEF groupName, listName, and writable file path
File path must include .xlsx extension for correct export format

d7NewEntries.title: RAMCOMMONLOGGER Custom Error Logger Object
d7NewEntries.principle: RAMCOMMONLOGGER is a project-specific PML object for logging macro errors and warnings to Excel files.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create via object RAMCOMMONLOGGER(), use addHeading() to set column headers, writeErrorDataToExcel() to dump log data.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_BI_tagRegister-export.pmlmac
!!ramCommonLogger = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
!headings = |Tag Name;Attribute Name;Error Text|
!!ramCommonLogger.addHeading(!headings.split(|;|))
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!rc = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()  -- use !! for global
!!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(!logFile, true)  -- second arg is append flag
pitfalls: Must be declared as global (!!) for cross-method access
addHeading expects semicolon-separated string that is split()
writeErrorDataToExcel second parameter controls append mode

d7NewEntries.title: MEASURE and UNIT Objects for Unit Conversion
d7NewEntries.principle: MEASURE and UNIT are PML system objects for working with engineering units and conversions.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create MEASURE('name') to get a measure object, then setunits(unit) to configure. Create UNIT('name') to get a unit reference.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB JDE_BI_tagRegister-export.pmlmac
!AngularFrequencyDimension = object MEASURE('AngularFrequency')
!rpmUnit = object UNIT(|rpm|)
!AngularFrequencyDimension.setunits(!rpmUnit)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
!measure = MEASURE('AngularFrequency')  -- missing OBJECT
!unit = UNIT('rpm')  -- missing OBJECT
pitfalls: Both MEASURE and UNIT require OBJECT keyword
setunits() may fail silently if unit is not valid for the measure
Unit names are case-sensitive

d7NewEntries.title: LSTDEF Collection Query Pattern
d7NewEntries.principle: PML1 'var !name collect all LSTDEF with (expression)' queries list definitions by name and returns a GRID collection.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |listName|)' to find a single list definition. Access via !grid.first().dbref() and !grid.size().
d7NewEntries.syntax:
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |IM-tag-dataset|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
  !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
  !gridRef.lstflt = !realUnset
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB RAMBiReportExport.pmlmac
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |IM-tag-dataset|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
  !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
  !gridRef.lstflt = !realUnset
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
var !grid collect all LSTDEF  -- missing 'with' filter
if (!grid.size() gt 0) then  -- should check eq 1 for uniqueness
pitfalls: LSTDEF query returns a GRID, not a single DBREF
Always check !grid.size() eq 1 before accessing first()
CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef extracts the list group name for export
$!gridRef uses query substitution, not direct method call

d7NewEntries.title: DBREF-to-PDMS-Object Attribute Access via .:  Syntax
d7NewEntries.principle: Use .:  (dot-colon) notation to access PDMS object attributes from a PML DBREF variable. Unlike .query() which returns attribute values as strings, .:  provides direct object reference access for nested attribute chains.
d7NewEntries.rule: After assigning a DBREF to a PML variable, use !dbref.:AttributeName to access any PDMS object attribute. Nested attributes chain with additional .: , e.g., !obj.:HavePartOutGoingConnections.[1].:RefConnectionsOut.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_46
!ces = !!collectallfor(|CE|, ||, world)
do !ce values !ces
  !!ce = !ce
  !terminals = !!ce.:HavePartTerminals
  !outConn   = !terminal.:HavePartOutGoingConnections
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- BAD: Using .query() for nested attributes
!attr = !ce.query(|HavePartOutGoingConnections|)
-- .query() returns a string, not a collection reference
pitfalls: .:  requires a valid PDMS object reference; a BADREF will throw an error
Unlike .query(), .:  returns the actual object/collection, not a string value
Attribute names are case-insensitive in PML but should follow AVEVA canonical casing
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PDMS Customization Guide — Object Attribute Access

d7NewEntries.title: object BLOCK(...) Constructor for Collection Evaluation
d7NewEntries.principle: Use object BLOCK(...) to create an inline code block that can be passed to collection methods like evaluate(). The block is evaluated once per collection element with the element referenced by the loop variable.
d7NewEntries.rule: Wrap a PML expression in object BLOCK(|expression|) to pass it as a block argument. Inside the block, use the loop variable name (e.g., !evalIndex) to access the current collection element.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_46
!markings = !channelTerminals.evaluate(
  object BLOCK(|!channelTerminals[!evalIndex].:marking[1]|)
)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- BAD: Passing a string instead of a block
!markings = !channelTerminals.evaluate('|!channelTerminals[!evalIndex].:marking[1]|')
pitfalls: The variable name inside object BLOCK must match the implicit iteration variable of the collection
object BLOCK(...) is not the same as a string expression — it creates a PML code block
Block variables are scoped to the evaluate() call

d7NewEntries.title: Canonical AVEVA PDMS Terminal and Connection Attribute Names
d7NewEntries.principle: PDMS objects use specific PascalCased attribute names for terminal and connection management. These attributes are case-insensitive in PML but should be referenced with canonical casing for consistency.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use the canonical attribute names listed below when accessing terminal and connection data on PDMS objects. Do not mix casing within a single codebase.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_46
!terminals = !!ce.:HavePartTerminals
!channels  = !!ce.:HavePartChannels
do !idx indices !terminals
  !terminal = !terminals[!idx]
  !channel  = !channels[!idx]
  !signals  = !terminal.:refPropagatedSignals
  !outConn  = !terminal.:HavePartOutGoingConnections
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- BAD: Inconsistent casing in same file
!terminals = !!ce.:HavePartTerminals
!chanTerms = !channel.:havepartchannelTerminals  -- should be HavePartChannelTerminals
!outConn   = !terminal.:Havepartoutgoingconnections  -- should be HavePartOutGoingConnections
pitfalls: Attribute names are case-insensitive in PML but inconsistent casing causes maintenance issues
Some attributes return collections (ARRAY/COLLECTION), others return single values
refPropagatedSignals may be unset() for terminals with no propagated signals
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PDMS Object Reference — Terminal and Connection Attributes

d7NewEntries.title: Case-Insensitive String Comparison with eqnocase()
d7NewEntries.principle: Use .eqnocase() method for case-insensitive string comparison. This is equivalent to .eq() but ignores letter case differences.
d7NewEntries.rule: Call .eqnocase(|value|) on a STRING object to compare against another string ignoring case. Returns TRUE if strings match regardless of case.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_46
!isIncomConn = !outConn[1].:RefConnectionsOut.acttype.eqnocase(|:IncomingConnection|)
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- BAD: Using .eq() for case-insensitive comparison
!isMatch = !str1.eq(|:incomingconnection|)  -- fails if case differs
pitfalls: eqnocase() is a STRING method; ensure the receiver is a STRING
Not available on non-string PML types
Use .eq() for case-sensitive comparison when needed

d7NewEntries.title: Nested DO/ENDDO with Indices Iteration and Collection.remove()
d7NewEntries.principle: When iterating over a collection by indices and conditionally removing elements, the loop index must account for shifting indices after removal. Using 'indices' in the DO clause captures the index set at loop entry time, but removing elements shifts subsequent indices.
d7NewEntries.rule: When using DO !idx indices !collection with conditional .remove(), be aware that removing element at !idx shifts all higher indices down by 1. Consider iterating in reverse or using a while loop with manual index control.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
do !idx indices !collection
  !ele = !collection[!idx]
  if (shouldRemove(!ele)) then
    !collection.remove(!idx)
    -- Note: higher indices have shifted!
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_46
do !d indices !incConn
  !ele = !incConn[!d]
  if (!refCon.unset()) then
    !incConn.remove(!d)
  else
    break
  endif
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- BAD: Assuming indices are stable after remove
-- This loop may skip elements or access invalid indices
pitfalls: remove() shifts all higher indices — elements may be skipped
Using 'indices' captures the index set at loop start; removed elements still have valid index values but point to different elements
break exits the entire loop, potentially leaving unprocessed elements

d7NewEntries.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
d7NewEntries.principle: PML RELOAD OBJECT reloads a previously compiled PML object into the current session, ensuring the latest definition is active.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT <ObjectName> to reload an object after its source has been modified. The object must already exist in the session.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Reload TAGMANAGEMENTTMP before using it
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.deleteUnnamedTags()
pitfalls: Reloading a non-existent object will cause a runtime error
Reloaded objects replace the previous instance in memory — existing references may become stale
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide — Macros section

d7NewEntries.title: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP customer object
d7NewEntries.principle: TAGMANAGEMENTTMP is a project-specific PML object providing tag management utilities including deletion of unnamed tags.
d7NewEntries.rule: Construct with object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP() and call deleteUnnamedTags() to remove unnamed tags from the current database context.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.deleteUnnamedTags()
pitfalls: Object must be reloaded after source changes
deleteUnnamedTags() operates on the current database session context

d7NewEntries.title: Dynamic Menu Creation in PML Forms
d7NewEntries.principle: PML forms support dynamic menu creation via !this.newMenu() and bar.add() methods, enabling runtime popup and bar menus.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use !this.newMenu('menuName') to create a menu object, then .add('callback', 'label', 'command') to add entries. Use !this.bar.add('category', 'name') for bar menu entries.
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Dynamic menu in form constructor
!this.bar.add('Tools', 'toolsMenu')
!toolsMenu = !this.newMenu('toolsMenu')
!toolsMenu.add('callback', 'Option 1', '!this.doOption1()')
!toolsMenu.add('callback', 'Option 2', '!this.doOption2()')
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Static menu defined at form setup (less flexible)
!menu = menu
!menu.add('Static', '.staticMethod')
pitfalls: Menu names must be unique within the form scope
Callback commands are strings, not method references
Bar menu categories appear as submenus
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide - Forms and Menus

d7NewEntries.title: DO VALUES Iteration over ARRAY Elements
d7NewEntries.principle: PML supports iterating over ARRAY elements using DO ... VALUES ... ENDDO, which yields each populated element as the loop index.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use DO !index VALUES !arrayName to iterate over all populated elements. !index holds the value of each element (not the position).
d7NewEntries.syntax:
DO !index VALUES !arrayName
  -- !index contains each element value
ENDDO
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Iterate over selected list items
!selectedItems = !this.list.val
do !index values !selectedItems
  !viewName = !this.list.rtext[!index]
  !this.processView(!viewName)
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using FROM/TO with array Size() when VALUES is more natural
!i = 1
do while !i.le(!selectedItems.Size())
  !index = !selectedItems[!i]
  !i = !i + 1
enddo
pitfalls: !index holds the element value, not the array index
Use !selectedItems[!index] to access array by value when values are indices
Array indices in PML start at 1
d7NewEntries.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide - Control Logic

d7NewEntries.title: defined() Check for Global Form Objects
d7NewEntries.principle: Use defined() to check if a global form object exists before attempting to access it, preventing runtime errors.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use if(defined(!!globalForm)) to check existence. If the form exists, access its methods; otherwise, create a new instance.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
if(defined(!!globalForm)) then
  !!globalForm.method()
else
  !!globalVar = object CLASS()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- Safe access to global logger form
if(defined(!!ramcommonloggerform)) then
  !!ramcommonloggerform.clearData()
else
  !!RAMCOMMONLOGGER = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Direct access without check (will error if form not loaded)
!!ramcommonloggerform.clearData()
pitfalls: defined() checks variable existence, not object validity
Global form names are case-insensitive in PML

d7NewEntries.title: FILE Object set() and exists() Pattern
d7NewEntries.principle: The FILE object requires .set() to resolve the path before .exists() can reliably check for the file or folder.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create FILE object with path, call .set() to resolve, then use .exists() to check. Combine with AND for conditional logic.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
!file = object FILE(!path)
if(!file.set() AND !file.exists()) then
  -- file/folder exists
else
  -- handle missing
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!file = object FILE(!outputFolder.val)
if(!file.set() AND !file.exists()) then
  -- proceed with export
else
  !!alert.warning('Please select valid output folder')
endif
d7NewEntries.exampleAntipattern:
-- Checking exists without set (may fail on relative paths)
!file = object FILE(!path)
if(!file.exists()) then
pitfalls: .set() resolves the path and returns success/failure
.exists() checks both files and folders
Use .fullname() to get resolved absolute path

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE Binding
d7NewEntries.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL from GridControl add-in can be bound to data via NETDATASOURCE object for dynamic data display.
d7NewEntries.rule: Create NETGRIDCONTROL object, configure properties (columnExcelFilter, fixedRows, etc.), create NETDATASOURCE with columns and rows, then bind with bindToDataSource().
d7NewEntries.syntax:
using namespace 'Aveva.Core.Presentation'
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.columnExcelFilter(true)
!grid.fixedRows(true)
!nds = object NETDATASOURCE('name', !headings, !rows)
!grid.bindToDataSource(!nds)
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
!this.gridSelectionList = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!this.coSelectionList.control = !this.gridSelectionList.handle()

d7NewEntries.title: Creating AVEVA tags via CREATEELEMENT and PMLElementManager
d7NewEntries.principle: AVEVA.Engineering.PMLElementManager CREATEELEMENT object can create tags with type and attributes.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use object CREATEELEMENT(), SetElementTypeByName(), AddAttributeValue(), Execute(), GetErrors() for tag creation with error handling via handle any/endhandle.
d7NewEntries.syntax:
using namespace |Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager|
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elem.SetElementTypeByName('|:$!typeName|')
!elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !tagName)
!elem.Execute()
!errors = !elem.GetErrors()
do !err values !errors
  !msg = !err.GetError()
enddo
d7NewEntries.exampleCanonical:
-- CB jackimform.pmlfrm
using namespace |Aveva.Engineering.PMLElementManager|
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()

handle any
  !this.logActions.append('|$!tag;Class [:$!cleanType] is not valid|')
  skip
endhandle

!elementNet.Execute()

d7NewEntries.title: NETDATASOURCE with Collection List data type
d7NewEntries.principle: NETDATASOURCE supports multiple data type strings including 'Collection List' for generic collection-based data binding.

  !headings = !!ramCommonLogger.getValidHeadingArrayFormat()
  !rows = !!ramCommonLogger.getValidLogArrayFormat()
  !nds = object NETDATASOURCE('Collection List', !headings, !rows)
  !this.gridLogList.bindToDataSource(!nds)
  !this.gridLogList.autoFitColumns()
endmethod
pitfalls: Using 'Collection List' with PDMS database queries will fail — use 'Piping', 'CABLE', etc. for DB queries.

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL.fixedRows() method
d7NewEntries.principle: The fixedRows() method pins the header rows so they remain visible during vertical scrolling.

-- CB ramCommonLoggerForm.pmlfrm

d7NewEntries.title: NETGRIDCONTROL.rowAddDeleteGrid() method
d7NewEntries.principle: The rowAddDeleteGrid() method enables inline row addition and deletion in the grid.

d7NewEntries.title: form-size anchor positioning keyword
d7NewEntries.principle: The 'form-size' keyword in anchor positioning references the full form dimensions, equivalent to the form's client area bounds.
d7NewEntries.rule: Use 'form-size' instead of ad-hoc expressions like 'form+1' for reliable form-relative positioning.

Do not mix form-size with numeric offsets without testing — form-size already accounts for form dimensions.
